We therefore propose Agent World Model in the Wild (WildAWM), a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks for training general computer-use agents (CUAs). Whereas existing approaches typically specialize in a single agent interaction interface, we construct executable environments that jointly support graphical user interfaces, model context protocol services, and command-line interfaces, allowing agents to flexibly combine visual interaction, tool use, and code execution. WildAWM is entirely powered by open-source models, demonstrating that high-quality computer-use environments can be generated without proprietary frontier models. Beyond environments, we address three recurring challenges in task synthesis: ensuring solvability, maintaining sufficient difficulty, and producing reliable verifiers, by introducing execution-based quality gates that combine heterogeneous agent rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, and counterfactual probes of judgment robustness. The resulting pipeline synthesizes 341 long-horizon environment-task pairs that can require over 100 agent steps to solve and remain challenging even for frontier models, with GPT-6-Astra solving only 60% of them. We train two Qwen models of different sizes exclusively in these synthetic worlds. Both models achieve substantial gains across 8 out-of-distribution benchmarks spanning web, claw, and computer-use agents, demonstrating that learning in WildAWM's synthesized worlds generalizes broadly to unseen computer-use tasks. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/MSR-Orchard/WildAWM.
items.title_ko: Agent World Model in the Wild: 컴퓨터 사용 에이전트 환경 합성
items.summary_ko: WildAWM(Agent World Model in the Wild)은 실제 컴퓨터 시스템에서 일반적인 컴퓨터 사용 에이전트(CUA)를 훈련하기 위한 제어 가능한 환경과 작업을 합성하는 확장 가능한 파이프라인을 제안합니다. 이는 실제 환경에서 직접 학습하는 것의 보안 위험을 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: 안전하고 확장 가능한 방식으로 실제 컴퓨터 환경에서 AI 에이전트를 훈련하는 방법을 제시하여, 실제 환경에 배포될 수 있는 강력한 AI 에이전트 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: KEEP-Bench: Evaluating Evidence Preservation in Context Compression
items.body: Context compression improves long-context efficiency but may introduce faithfulness issues through an information bottleneck. Existing evaluations rely on QA metrics, but a reader can still answer correctly from an unfaithful compression, so these metrics underestimate such loss. To bridge this gap, we introduce KEEP-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark that directly assesses compression faithfulness with 4,102 cases across three challenging settings that require keeping evidence for plausible reference resolutions, explicit qualifiers, and minority perspectives. Experiments show that even with tailored prompting, the strongest models remain unreliable: despite context windows exceeding 100K tokens and inputs averaging only 3.1K tokens, the best open-weight model (31B) preserves all required evidence in only 66.8% of cases, and the best proprietary model in only 61.6%. Performance also varies sharply across evidence structures, so conclusions from limited structures may be biased. We further introduce a metric, Evidence Preservation Return (EPR), to relate evidence recall to inference FLOPs, and find that it peaks at moderate scales (4B-8B), where recall remains low. Additional output budget mainly benefits already strong models and widens capability gaps, yet the stronger preservation of these models comes at a steep computational cost. These findings highlight the importance for future work to investigate compressors with strong information preservation under a small computation budget, rather than relying on a large output budget or model scaling.
items.title_ko: KEEP-Bench: 컨텍스트 압축에서의 증거 보존 평가
items.summary_ko: KEEP-Bench는 컨텍스트 압축이 정보 병목 현상을 통해 충실성 문제를 야기할 수 있음을 지적하며, 압축의 충실성을 직접 평가하는 진단 벤치마크를 소개합니다. 기존 QA 메트릭이 정보 손실을 과소평가할 수 있다는 점을 보완합니다.
items.why_ko: 긴 컨텍스트 처리의 효율성을 높이는 컨텍스트 압축 기술의 한계를 명확히 하고, 정보의 정확성과 충실성을 유지하는 데 필요한 새로운 평가 방법을 제시합니다.

items.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development
items.body: Beyond basic tool use and coding skills, effectively incorporating visual references into agentic generation is equally essential for applying AI agents to real-world productivity tasks. We study this crucial capability through webpage development, a practical and readily evaluable setting in which existing benchmarks remain largely idealized: they typically focus on reconstructing visual targets or generating webpages from textual instructions alone, overlooking the more common workflow of developing from visual examples. Specifically, we introduce RefCraft, a benchmark comprising 300 realistic multimodal webpage-development tasks that combine natural-language instructions with screenshots from one to five reference webpages. Agents must selectively interpret and utilize these references while rendering, visually inspecting, and iteratively refining their outputs. We evaluate the resulting open-ended artifacts using independently verifiable keypoints and complementary programmatic and VLM judges. Across nine frontier (M)LLMs, the strongest system achieves an overall score of only 52.12 out of 100, revealing that visual-reference-conditioned agentic generation remains a substantial challenge for current models in practical webpage-development settings.
items.title_ko: RefCraft: 웹 개발을 통한 시각 참조 조건 에이전트 생성 벤치마킹
items.summary_ko: RefCraft는 웹 페이지 개발을 통해 시각적 참조를 효과적으로 통합하는 에이전트 생성 능력을 벤치마킹합니다. 기존 벤치마크가 이상화되어 있거나 텍스트 명령에만 초점을 맞추는 한계를 넘어 실제 작업 흐름을 반영합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 시각적 정보를 활용하여 실제 세계의 생산성 작업을 수행하는 능력을 평가하고 향상시키는 데 중요한 벤치마크입니다.

items.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
items.body: Memory-native evolution requires making memory an intrinsic capability of foundation models, enabling them to continuously accumulate and utilize information. To this end, we introduce MemT-1.0, a new architecture of memory foundation models that internalize memory as part of model computation. Building on Metis, MemT-1.0 employs Gated DeltaNet-2 with a stable token-level memory update mechanism within each turn. We further introduce Mixture-of-Storage to scale native memory capacity. Following a deliberate backbone preparation, we develop a two-stage training pipeline consisting of continued pre-training and post-training, supported by 34B tokens of training data and efficient training and inference infrastructure. We release a model family comprising MemT-1.0-Nano and MemT-1.0-Flash, and conduct a comprehensive evaluation of memory and general capabilities. The results show that they outperform the parametric memory baselines on average and remain competitive with retrieval-augmented methods, while largely preserving general capabilities. At a history length of 128K tokens, MemT-1.0-Nano achieves approximately $1.86\times$ end-to-end inference speedup and a $66\times$ reduction in persistent storage relative to full context KV cache. By internalizing retrieved procedural experience, MemT-1.0 improves task success on agentic tasks, providing a practical step toward memory-native evolution.
items.title_ko: MemT-1.0: 메모리 기반 진화를 향하여
items.summary_ko: MemT-1.0은 파운데이션 모델의 내재적 능력으로 메모리를 통합하여 지속적으로 정보를 축적하고 활용할 수 있도록 하는 새로운 아키텍처입니다. Gated DeltaNet-2와 Mixture-of-Storage를 통해 메모리 용량을 확장합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델이 지속적으로 학습하고 기억을 활용할 수 있게 하는 '메모리 기반 진화'는 더욱 지능적이고 적응력 있는 AI 시스템을 만드는 데 중요한 발전입니다.

items.title: SpecMRL: Redesign Matryoshka Representation Learning within Parametric Spectrum
items.body: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) is designed to support flexible representation sizes by jointly optimizing nested prefixes. While effective, this design lacks an explicit constraint to ensure that the leading portion provides a suitable compact encoding. To address this, we propose SpecMRL, which reorganizes the feature space to enable more effective prefix readout. Specifically, we extend MRL with a parameter-derived spectral basis organized with feature importance. SpecMRL otherwise follows standard MRL, with prefix readout performed in the learned spectral space. Experiments on MTEB show that SpecMRL outperforms MRL at all evaluated reduced dimensions, with larger gains under more aggressive compression. These results suggest that the learned spectral basis better prioritizes informative directions, enabling more effective representation compression. Notably, SpecMRL extends the performance frontier of MRL, surpassing full-dimensional MRL with only half the embedding dimensions.
items.title_ko: SpecMRL: 매트료시카 표현 학습의 파라메트릭 스펙트럼 재설계
items.summary_ko: SpecMRL은 Matryoshka Representation Learning(MRL)의 기능을 확장하여, 피처 공간을 재구성하고 파라미터 기반 스펙트럼 기저를 활용하여 보다 효과적인 접두사 읽기를 가능하게 합니다. 이는 표현 학습의 효율성을 높입니다.
items.why_ko: 다양한 크기의 표현을 유연하게 지원하는 MRL의 한계를 극복하고, 정보 압축 및 효율적인 표현 학습에 새로운 방향을 제시합니다.

items.title: AfriBED: a Speech Recognition Bias Evaluation Dataset for Low Resource African Languages
items.body: Despite advancements in automatic speech recognition systems (ASR), current systems exhibit speaker-attribute bias, i.e., their speech recognition performance is biased against certain speakers based on their demographic attributes such as gender, accents, and speaker type. However, accurately assessing speaker attribute bias in a given ASR system requires the availability of a bias evaluation dataset with comparable speech across subgroups of a speaker attribute. In this paper, we introduce African speech Bias Evaluation Dataset (AfriBED), a novel speech recognition bias evaluation dataset for two low resource African languages, Bemba and Nyanja, to detect and estimate gender and speaker-type bias for ASR systems. The dataset comprises 9 hours of speech with 3928 utterances recorded by 80 speakers for Bemba, while the Nyanja set includes 6260 utterances with approximately 18 hours of speech recorded by 127 speakers. The results of our baseline experiments demonstrate that the datasets are useful for examining gender and speaker-type attribute bias in the target languages.
items.title_ko: AfriBED: 저자원 아프리카 언어 ASR 편향 평가 데이터셋
items.summary_ko: AfriBED는 저자원 아프리카 언어의 자동 음성 인식(ASR) 시스템에 대한 화자 속성 편향을 평가하기 위한 데이터셋입니다. 이는 특정 인구 통계학적 속성에 대한 ASR 시스템의 편향 문제를 해결하는 데 기여합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 시스템의 편향 문제를 해결하고 소외된 언어 커뮤니티를 위한 포괄적인 ASR 시스템 개발에 필수적인 자원입니다.

items.title: ASTOR: Benchmarking and Improving Autoformulation for Soft-Constraint Optimization with a Formal Grammar
items.body: Real-world decision problems combine two qualitatively different kinds of constraints: requirements that must be satisfied, called hard constraints, and preferences that can be violated, called soft constraints. Because these problems are often posed to decision-makers in natural language, large language models offer a natural tool for assisting with their solution. This has given rise to autoformulation, which focuses on using LLMs to translate natural-language descriptions of decision problems into executable mathematical optimization models. However, this research often neglects soft constraints like those proposed by consumers, managers, and planners, despite the fact that many practical problems require modeling them explicitly. We introduce ASTOR, an inference-time framework that maps a natural-language decision problem to a grammar-guided abstract syntax tree (AST) before deterministically compiling the resulting representation into executable optimization code. We also introduce SoftOR, a unified benchmark of natural language problems which focuses on soft constraint formulations. On SoftOR, ASTOR achieves the best aggregate accuracy among comparable single-request and multi-agent LLM methods while remaining competitive on standard autoformulation benchmarks that include only hard constraints. Code and data are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/astor-softor-iclr-E34C/README.md.
items.title_ko: ASTOR: 공식 문법을 활용한 소프트 제약 최적화 자동 포뮬러 벤치마킹 및 개선
items.summary_ko: ASTOR는 실세계 의사 결정 문제에서 발생하는 '하드 제약'과 '소프트 제약'을 LLM이 자연어 설명에서 자동으로 공식화하는 능력을 벤치마킹하고 개선합니다. 이는 최적화 문제의 AI 기반 해결에 중점을 둡니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 복잡한 의사 결정 문제를 더 정확하고 효율적으로 자동 공식화할 수 있도록 돕는 연구로, 다양한 산업 분야에서의 AI 활용을 확장시킵니다.

items.title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting
items.body: Next Best Action (NBA) systems must select among customer interventions (e.g., discounts, promotions, and lifecycle actions), maximize long-term economic value, satisfy complex operational constraints, and remain causally grounded. Existing approaches lack a rigorous framework for meeting these requirements jointly. We address this gap by formulating NBA as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP). We then integrate off-policy causal correction of the estimated customer dynamics directly into the Linear Programming (LP) formulation of the CMDP. The resulting policy selects actions based on customer states to maximize long-term value while explicitly enforcing business guardrails. Furthermore, the LP formulation yields shadow prices that quantify the economic trade-offs of operational constraints (e.g., fairness and user welfare), enhancing policy interpretability. We validate our proposed offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework on an industry case study involving rideshare coupon targeting, where customer states are defined by Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) stages. We evaluate performance using model-based off-policy evaluation, with causal dynamics estimated from a temporal holdout. Under the observed coupon budget and RFM state representation, our optimized policy improves customer lifetime value (LTV) by 19% over the estimated behavior policy and 8% over a myopic baseline. Although the demonstrated action space is binary, the proposed framework is action-agnostic, yielding a general-purpose decision module for targeting systems that manage multiple interventions.
items.title_ko: Next Best Action: 비즈니스 행동 타겟팅을 위한 인과성 제약 오프라인 RL
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 Next Best Action(NBA) 시스템을 인과성 제약 마르코프 의사 결정 과정(CMDP)으로 공식화하여, 장기적인 경제적 가치를 극대화하고 복잡한 운영 제약을 만족하며 인과적으로 근거 있는 행동을 선택하도록 합니다. 오프라인 인과적 교정 기법을 통합합니다.
items.why_ko: 비즈니스 환경에서 AI 기반 의사 결정 시스템이 장기적인 가치와 운영 제약을 모두 고려하여 최적의 행동을 선택하도록 돕는 중요한 방법론입니다.

items.title: Safety Mid-Training: Internalizing LLM Safety as a Foundational Capability
items.body: Safety alignment for large language models (LLMs) is primarily performed during post-training, while recent work has also begun incorporating safety data into pre-training. Yet safety can degrade when later training no longer includes safety data, and gains in safety often come at the cost of general capability. This tension suggests that safety and general reasoning should not be treated as separate training goals. We instead view safety as an LLM capability that can be learned through a reasoning structure shared with general tasks. Both require the model to understand intent or task goals, apply relevant knowledge, and reason about potential consequences. We introduce safety mid-training, a stage between pre-training and post-training that jointly develops safety and general reasoning through this shared structure. Given safety and utility prompts, the base model generates structured documents and reasoning traces that are then used for mid-training. Safety mid-training reduces average attack success rate (ASR) by 72% to 81% relative to Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B base models, while also improving general capability. The benefits persist through subsequent post-training. After general-only SFT, mid-trained models largely retain their safety, achieving lower ASR than the baselines without sacrificing general capability. They also retain safety under general-only GRPO without safety rewards, while subsequent RL reaches a better safety-utility frontier when initialized from the mid-trained models. Together, these results suggest that learning safety and general reasoning within a shared mid-training stage can reduce the safety-utility trade-off and make safety more robust to subsequent training.
items.body_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)의 안전 정렬은 주로 사후 학습 중에 수행되며, 최근 연구에서는 사전 학습에도 안전 데이터를 통합하기 시작했습니다. 그러나 이후 학습에 안전 데이터가 더 이상 포함되지 않으면 안전성이 저하될 수 있으며, 안전성 향상은 종종 일반적인 능력 저하를 수반합니다. 이러한 갈등은 안전성과 일반적인 추론을 별개의 학습 목표로 취급해서는 안 된다는 것을 시사합니다. 우리는 대신 안전성을 일반적인 작업과 공유하는 추론 구조를 통해 학습할 수 있는 LLM 능력으로 간주합니다. 둘 다 모델이 의도나 작업 목표를 이해하고, 관련 지식을 적용하며, 잠재적인 결과에 대해 추론해야 합니다. 우리는 사전 학습과 사후 학습 사이의 단계인 안전 중간 학습(safety mid-training)을 도입하여 이 공유 구조를 통해 안전성과 일반 추론을 공동으로 개발합니다. 안전 및 유틸리티 프롬프트가 주어지면, 기본 모델은 구조화된 문서와 추론 추적을 생성하며, 이는 중간 학습에 사용됩니다. 안전 중간 학습은 Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, 8B 기본 모델에 비해 평균 공격 성공률(ASR)을 72%에서 81%까지 감소시키면서 일반적인 능력도 향상시킵니다. 이러한 이점은 후속 사후 학습을 통해서도 지속됩니다. 일반 전용 SFT 후, 중간 학습된 모델은 안전성을 크게 유지하며, 일반적인 능력을 희생하지 않고 기준선보다 낮은 ASR을 달성합니다. 또한 안전 보상 없이 일반 전용 GRPO에서도 안전성을 유지하며, 중간 학습된 모델에서 초기화될 때 후속 RL은 더 나은 안전-유틸리티 프론티어에 도달합니다. 종합적으로 이러한 결과는 공유 중간 학습 단계 내에서 안전성과 일반 추론을 학습하는 것이 안전-유틸리티 상충 관계를 줄이고 안전성을 후속 학습에 더 강건하게 만들 수 있음을 시사합니다.
items.title_ko: 훈련 중 안전: LLM 안전성을 기초 역량으로 내재화
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 LLM의 안전성 정렬이 주로 후처리 단계에서 이루어지지만, 안전성을 일반적인 능력과 분리된 목표로 보지 않고 훈련 중 reasoning을 통해 학습 가능한 기초 역량으로 내재화해야 한다고 주장합니다. 이는 안전성 향상이 일반 역량 저하로 이어지는 문제를 해결하려 합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 안전성을 핵심 역량으로 통합하는 접근 방식은 더욱 견고하고 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 시스템을 구축하는 데 필수적이며, 안전성 연구의 중요한 방향을 제시합니다.

items.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
items.body: Brain encoding models aim to predict neural responses to stimuli. The most widely used approach fits readouts from frozen pretrained backbones. Using neural data to train large models from scratch or fully fine-tune them after task-pretraining has proven difficult because neural data is costly and limited. We show that parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) enables us to effectively adapt very large pretrained backbones for brain encoding with a small number of trainable parameters. To make it computationally practical, we exploit the backbone's causal structure to predict multiple timepoints in a single pass instead of using sliding windows, significantly reducing feature-extraction cost. This enables efficient fine-tuning of multimodal backbones with up to 104B parameters, the largest model adapted for brain encoding to our knowledge. Trained with a low-rank adapter (LoRA) and a lightweight readout, our approach consistently improves brain encoding performance across nine diverse multimodal backbones. On the same Qwen3-Omni backbone as the prior state-of-the-art (SoTA), our method BrainLoRA achieves the best published performance on the Algonauts 2025 Challenge. We also show the adapted multimodal backbones remain interpretable: modality attribution recovers the canonical sensory topography that prior work often obtains by construction from separate unimodal encoders, and neural adaptation increases the contribution of audio inputs and cross-modal mixing within the backbone. To scale out the number of adapted models, we develop a multi-LoRA kernel that accelerates joint training of multiple LoRAs on a shared backbone. This enables an ensemble of 200+ adapted models that ranks first on the public Algonauts post-challenge leaderboard at the time of writing. Together, our results highlight PEFT as an efficient and powerful paradigm for brain encoding.
items.title_ko: 뇌 인코딩을 위한 파라미터 효율적인 미세 조정 스케일링
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 뇌 인코딩 모델에서 신경 데이터 훈련의 어려움을 해결하기 위해 파라미터 효율적인 미세 조정(PEFT)이 대규모 사전 훈련된 백본을 효과적으로 적응시킬 수 있음을 보여줍니다. 이는 적은 수의 훈련 가능한 파라미터로도 높은 성능을 달성합니다.
items.why_ko: 제한된 신경 데이터로도 대규모 모델을 뇌 인코딩 작업에 효과적으로 적용할 수 있는 방법을 제시하여, 뇌 과학과 AI의 융합 연구를 가속화합니다.

items.title: Mise-en-Video: Fine-Grained 3D Control for Multi-Shot Video Generation
items.body: Recent advances in text-to-video generation have enabled high-fidelity single-shot synthesis, yet practical storytelling creation requires multi-shot videos with both strong inter-shot consistency and fine-grained controllability. Existing multi-shot video generation approaches achieve strong consistency but still fall short in controllability. In this paper, we propose Mise-en-Video (MeV), a highly controllable multi-shot video generation framework that allows video creators to conduct staging the multi-shot in the 3D space and then generate the corresponding multi-shot video. To achieve this, our framework combines a hierarchical attention mechanism for multi-level narrative consistency with 3D-aware layout guidance for precise, per-shot spatial control. To support training and evaluation, we develop standardized annotation pipelines and construct a 160K-video dataset with hierarchical multi-shot texts and oriented 3D bounding boxes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MeV consistently outperforms strong baselines in video quality, inter-shot consistency, and subject-level controllability.
items.title_ko: Mise-en-Video: 다중 샷 비디오 생성을 위한 정교한 3D 제어
items.summary_ko: Mise-en-Video (MeV)는 강력한 샷 간 일관성과 정교한 제어 가능성을 모두 제공하는 다중 샷 비디오 생성 프레임워크입니다. 이는 텍스트-비디오 생성의 발전을 통해 실용적인 스토리텔링 콘텐츠 제작을 가능하게 합니다.
items.why_ko: 단일 샷을 넘어 여러 샷으로 구성된 비디오를 일관성 있게 생성하고 정교하게 제어하는 기술은 영화, 광고 등 콘텐츠 제작 분야에 혁신을 가져올 잠재력이 있습니다.

items.title: Learning to Refer: Inference-Time Collaboration in Decentralized Federated Learning
items.body: In decentralized federated learning, heterogeneous clients may develop complementary expertise, yet each query is typically evaluated only by the client where it arrives. To exploit this distributed expertise without global coordination, we formulate inference-time collaboration as budgeted local expert referral, a graph-constrained routing process in which a query can move only between neighboring clients and only visited clients contribute to its final prediction. EdgeDRM implements this framework by learning a density-based routing potential for each client: differences between neighboring potentials provide the comparisons used to select successive referrals, while local task models generate predictions that are aggregated along the resulting route. Both training and inference are decentralized, using only neighbor-local information without a central router or graph-wide client scoring. We establish estimation guarantees for the learned comparisons and characterize how local improvement and graph structure govern prior-weighted density gains from referral. Experiments on benchmark and real-world medical data show that EdgeDRM outperforms graph-matched decentralized baselines in most settings, with the clearest benefits under sparse connectivity.
items.title_ko: Learning to Refer: 분산형 연합 학습의 추론 시간 협업
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 분산형 연합 학습에서 이질적인 클라이언트들이 상호 보완적인 전문 지식을 개발할 수 있지만, 각 쿼리가 도착한 클라이언트에서만 평가되는 문제를 지적합니다. 이를 해결하기 위해 추론 시간 협업을 예산 제약이 있는 로컬 전문가 추천으로 공식화합니다.
items.why_ko: 분산된 AI 시스템에서 클라이언트 간의 지식 공유 및 협업을 최적화하여, 연합 학습의 효율성과 성능을 향상시키는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Teacher Supervision, Fixed Representations and Calibration: Exact Risk Calculations for Candidate-Scoring Decision Models
items.body: Candidate-scoring decision models return a probability distribution over a presented set of answers. Public documentation of one such system, Jev, and of an open counterpart, JevAny, describes three training ingredients that determine what these probabilities estimate: soft targets from larger models, a frozen pretrained backbone and temperature calibration. We analyze each ingredient in Gaussian surrogates where the finite-sample risk can be computed exactly. A student trained on teacher targets inherits the teacher's bias, which more student data does not remove and agreement with the teacher does not reveal. A fixed representation lowers the risk only below an explicit sample-size threshold. In a probit model the exact recalibration map is a temperature scaling, which removes all excess risk only when the teacher's coefficient has the correct direction and otherwise leaves a residual that calibration diagnostics do not detect. Under Luce's choice axiom, candidate scores are coherent across refinements of an event if and only if they aggregate by log-sum-exp. On 231,521 credit card complaints from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, where the decision is whether a complaint ends in monetary relief, a student trained on a logistic teacher's probabilities ends at the teacher's decision cost while a student trained on outcomes goes 8% below it, a 30B model read zero-shot remains worse than the teacher after recalibration, and that model departs from the coherence condition by 17.5 decibans. Pretrained representations reduce the labeled data required and calibration corrects the scale of the probabilities, but neither corrects a biased teacher, so the probabilities have to be checked against realized outcomes.
items.title_ko: 교사 감독, 고정된 표현 및 보정: 후보 점수 매기기 결정 모델에 대한 정확한 위험 계산
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 후보 점수 매기기 결정 모델의 세 가지 훈련 요소(대규모 모델의 소프트 타겟, 고정된 사전 훈련 백본, 온도 보정)가 확률 추정에 미치는 영향을 가우스 대리 모델에서 정확한 위험 계산을 통해 분석합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델의 예측 신뢰도를 높이고, 다양한 훈련 구성 요소가 모델 성능에 미치는 영향을 정량적으로 이해하는 데 중요한 통찰력을 제공합니다.

items.title: Two hidden layer suffice: the caterpillar net
items.body: Every continuous piecewise linear (CPWL) function is a finite signed sum of maxima of affine functions, making maximum representation a central problem in the study of the expressiveness of ReLU networks. A now-disproved conjecture predicted logarithmic depth for maxima. Inspired by the proof by Brunck et al. (2026) that two hidden layers suffice for general CPWL functions, we give the Caterpillar Net, a nonrecursive construction for the maximum of $N$ inputs with two hidden layers of widths $O(N^2)$ and $2^{O(N\log N)}$. The construction has a direct geometric interpretation.
items.title_ko: 두 개의 은닉층으로 충분하다: 캐터필러 넷
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 두 개의 은닉층으로 충분한 너비 $O(\log N/\log\log N)$를 가진 ReLU 네트워크가 임의의 연속적인 조각 선형(CPWL) 함수를 표현할 수 있음을 보여주는 '캐터필러 넷'을 소개합니다. 이는 최대 함수 표현에 대한 깊이 제약을 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: 신경망의 표현력에 대한 이론적 이해를 심화하고, 효율적인 네트워크 아키텍처 설계에 중요한 기초 지식을 제공합니다.

items.title: On Data Scaling in Tabular ML: More Data, Better Generalization?
items.body: Recent work in tabular machine learning has emphasized the importance of diverse and realistic evaluation settings. The niche of large-scale (1M+) data, however, remains under-explored. To study training-data scaling, we assemble eight real-world tabular datasets with up to around ten million training examples, retaining the natural distribution shifts of the tasks and using random-split evaluation as a control. We find that GBDTs and MLP-based models show broadly similar scaling trends, with gains from both additional training data and algorithmic improvements. Tabular foundation models show more varied scaling behavior, with recent versions benefiting more consistently from larger contexts even under distribution shift. However, scaling training data under distribution shift introduces new challenges: in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance mostly improve together at smaller scales but can diverge at larger scales. We examine this through MLP capacity sweeps and comparisons of the validation distributions used for tuning and early stopping in MLPs and GBDTs. We also compare common practices of using validation data, contrasting its use for model selection in MLP pipelines with using it for in-context fitting in tabular foundation model pipelines. Under stronger shifts, MLPs selected using validation representative of the evaluation conditions generally maintain or improve performance as training data grows. In contrast, including such examples in context improves foundation-model performance, but does not prevent deterioration with increasing training size in our experiments.
items.title_ko: 테이블형 ML 데이터 스케일링: 데이터가 많을수록 일반화가 잘 될까?
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 대규모(1M+) 테이블형 데이터에서 데이터 스케일링이 모델 일반화에 미치는 영향을 탐구합니다. GBDT와 MLP 기반 모델이 유사한 스케일링 경향을 보이며, 더 많은 데이터가 항상 더 나은 일반화로 이어지지 않을 수 있음을 시사합니다.
items.why_ko: 테이블형 데이터셋에서 데이터 증가가 모델 성능에 미치는 영향을 실증적으로 분석하여, 데이터 중심 AI 개발 전략 수립에 실질적인 가이드라인을 제공합니다.

items.title: SOMA: Continuous Monitoring and Intervention for System Two Reasoning with System One Models
items.body: Reasoning models often run into problems without noticing them, even when symptoms are visible in their own text. In humans, metacognition separates monitoring from control: fast, intuitive signals keep watch while slow, deliberate reasoning unfolds and help decide whether to continue, change course, or stop. System One (S1) decision models, such as Jev, are a natural candidate for this role: they return a calibrated probability for a natural-language question about a text in one fast call, yet they are used only as gates before reasoning. We introduce SOMA (System One Metacognitive Awareness), in which an S1 model continuously monitors a System Two (S2) reasoning model and intervenes when needed. SOMA has three layers: a scenario layer states each objective in natural language with predefined actions, an awareness layer lets S1 judge whether the described behavior appears, and a control layer accumulates these judgments, first reminds S2, and takes over only if the behavior persists. Sharing one S1 model and one controller across tasks, without training, SOMA addresses two different failures on two reasoning models: on overthinking, it cuts reasoning tokens by up to 36\% while improving average accuracy, and on unanswerable questions, it raises abstention from 70.5\% to 87.2\%.
items.title_ko: SOMA: 시스템 원 모델로 시스템 투 추론에 대한 지속적인 모니터링 및 개입
items.summary_ko: SOMA는 추론 모델이 문제를 인식하지 못할 때 시스템 원(System One) 결정 모델(예: Jev)을 사용하여 지속적으로 모니터링하고 개입하는 프레임워크입니다. 이는 빠르고 직관적인 신호를 활용하여 느리고 신중한 추론 과정에 대한 감독을 제공합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 자기 인식 및 오류 감지 능력을 향상시켜, 복잡한 추론 과정에서 발생할 수 있는 오류를 줄이고 모델의 신뢰성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Training with ML-labeled Data via Stochastic First- and Zeroth-Order Optimization
items.body: Training a machine learning (ML) model is an optimization process that typically requires a set of examples with ground-truth labels beforehand. Obtaining these ground truths usually requires laborious human effort and can be costly. The scalability of human labeling becomes a concern when there are a large number of data points that need to be labeled. To address this practical issue, we consider an optimization setting where a subset of samples has ground-truth labels, while the remaining data points were labeled by an ML predictor, which could potentially assign incorrect labels to those points. We propose both first-order and zeroth-order stochastic optimization methods for training on datasets consisting of a mix of true-labeled and ML-labeled samples. We further conduct comprehensive empirical studies from training a linear regression model to fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for training with ML-labeled data.
items.title_ko: 확률적 1차 및 0차 최적화를 통한 ML-레이블 데이터 학습
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 일부 샘플에만 실제 레이블이 있고 나머지는 기계 학습(ML)으로 레이블링된 데이터로 모델을 훈련하는 최적화 설정을 다룹니다. 확률적 1차 및 0차 최적화를 통해 이러한 실제 문제를 해결하는 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 대규모 데이터셋에서 수동 레이블링 비용을 줄이면서도 효과적으로 모델을 훈련할 수 있는 방법을 제시하여, 데이터 부족 문제를 겪는 개발자들에게 실용적인 해결책을 제공합니다.

items.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Market Making on Prediction-Market Order Books
items.body: A market maker provides liquidity by quoting prices to buy and sell an asset, earning the spread while managing inventory risk. We study market makers trained with multi-agent reinforcement learning on prediction markets, specifically Polymarket, whose thin order books pose distinct challenges. Three challenges underpin this research: adverse selection may cause a policy trained on real data to stop quoting; the consequences of a quote can arrive many steps after the action; and prediction-market L2 data does not identify individual orders needed for simulation. We address these challenges by reconstructing order-level LOBSTER-format data from Polymarket and training agents in JaxMARL-HFT on 417 real markets. We enrich the baseline market maker's observation space with the book and recent flow, redesign its actions and inventory controls, and propose a cooperative multi-agent decomposition into a quoter and a risk manager trained using recurrent Independent Proximal Policy Optimisation (IPPO) with RNN policies. We investigate reward shaping, particularly reward blending and post-fill markout, to mitigate credit-assignment difficulties between the agents. Our redesigned single-agent market maker quotes more frequently and incurs smaller held-out losses than the retrained JaxMARL-HFT baseline, although the contributions of jointly changed observations, actions and risk constraints are not separately identified. Decomposition alone performs poorly; careful reward design substantially improves the desk relative to the unshaped split and yields our best result. Models are evaluated on realised end-of-episode portfolio value on held-out markets. None establishes positive average portfolio value in periodic held-out evaluation, and each configuration was trained with one seed. The environment, data and protocol lay a foundation for makers that quote many linked markets at once.
items.title_ko: 예측 시장 호가창에서의 시장 조성을 위한 협력적 다중 에이전트 강화 학습
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 예측 시장에서 시장 조성을 위해 다중 에이전트 강화 학습을 활용하는 방법을 연구합니다. 이는 예측 시장의 얇은 호가창, 지연된 행동 결과, 예측 시장 특유의 불확실성 등 세 가지 주요 과제를 다룹니다.
items.why_ko: AI가 금융 시장, 특히 예측 시장과 같은 복잡하고 동적인 환경에서 효율적인 전략을 학습하고 실행하는 능력을 보여줍니다.

items.title: LG-Bench: A Graph-Structured Evaluation Benchmark for Life Sciences
items.body: Traditional evaluation benchmarks reduce inherently interconnected scientific knowledge in life sciences into flat lists of questions, disregarding the underlying topological structure of the knowledge. We introduce, the first graph-structured benchmark for life sciences, featuring over 10,000 high-quality multiple-choice questions across medicine, biology, and chemistry. Our approach constructs a weighted evaluation graph using bidirectional matching and semantic similarity algorithms, where nodes represent questions and edge weights capture their semantic relationships. Leveraging this graph topology, we design two novel evaluation metrics. The Global Coherence Score (GCS) measures a model's consistency within semantically related neighborhoods, while Knowledge Balance Score (KBS) analyzes how model errors are distributed across the graph to reveal conceptual blind spots. LG-Bench facilitates fine-grained comparison of LLMs by surfacing differences in conceptual coherence and patterns of knowledge organization across models. Our framework shifts the evaluation paradigm from flat accuracy metrics to structure-aware analysis, offering a new lens for diagnosing and improving LLM performance in the life sciences domain.
items.title_ko: LG-Bench: 생명 과학을 위한 그래프 구조 평가 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: LG-Bench는 생명 과학 분야의 내재적으로 상호 연결된 지식을 평가하기 위한 최초의 그래프 구조 벤치마크입니다. 이는 10,000개 이상의 고품질 객관식 질문을 통해 기존 벤치마크의 한계를 극복합니다.
items.why_ko: 생명 과학 분야에서 AI 모델의 복잡한 지식 추론 능력을 정확하게 평가할 수 있는 새로운 표준을 제시하여, 바이오 AI 연구 발전에 기여합니다.

items.title: RESIN: Multi-Chain Reasoning with Entity-Structured Indexing
items.body: Multi-chain reasoning is a challenging task not only because the multi-chain evidence is dispersed, but also because different parts of reasoning may require distinct, interacting chains of support. Flat retrieval can flood a model with loosely related text, whereas early selection of a single reasoning path can discard evidence that becomes useful only after other facts are considered. We introduce RESIN (Reasoning with Entity Structured Indexing), which uses structure to locate evidence while keeping the original source as the basis for reasoning. RESIN decomposes a question into focused one-hop needs, retrieves a small set of source-grounded units for each hop, and places only this relevant evidence in a compact reasoning buffer. The buffer preserves alternative supports until final composition, making intermediate decisions explicit without forcing a brittle path. On the full HolisQA benchmark, RESIN achieves 82.92 context recall and 76.70 answer relevancy over all questions, with higher reported CR and AR across five domains and higher F1 in four domains than the published baselines. Ablations show that both typed evidence diversity and hop-wise decomposition are essential, supporting a clear conclusion: Precise evidence organization and delayed commitment make multi-chain reasoning effective and auditable. Our code is available at https://github.com/RamonMeng/RESIN.
items.title_ko: RESIN: 엔티티 구조 인덱싱을 이용한 멀티체인 추론
items.summary_ko: RESIN(Reasoning with Entity Structured Indexing)은 멀티체인 추론의 어려움을 해결하기 위해 엔티티 구조 인덱싱을 사용하여 증거를 찾아내는 방법을 제안합니다. 이는 분산된 증거와 상호 작용하는 다양한 추론 체인을 효과적으로 관리합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 복잡한 멀티체인 추론 작업을 더 정확하고 효율적으로 수행하도록 돕는 중요한 기술로, 복잡한 정보 검색 및 답변 생성 시스템 개발에 유용합니다.

items.title: Game of Phones: Harnessing Game Theory and LLMs in 'Bot Wars' to Counteract Phone Scams
items.body: Phone scams impose substantial and growing costs on individuals and financial systems worldwide, yet existing countermeasures impose no resource cost on perpetrators. Strategic scam-baiting, in which automated agents engage scammers to deplete their operational capacity, offers a proactive alternative but requires dynamic strategy adaptation that static systems cannot provide. We introduce a game-theoretic framework enabling LLMs to learn effective counter-strategies through in-context experience without fine-tuning. The framework models scammer-baiter interactions as a two-player game with empirically grounded strategies and utility functions, using Nash equilibrium as a formal benchmark for evaluating learned behaviour. Across 300 simulated dialogues and three LLM architectures, adaptive strategy selection achieves 28.9-79.7% closer alignment to Nash equilibrium than non-adaptive baselines. The code and an annotated dataset of 300 dialogues with turn-level strategy labels and utility scores are released at https://github.com/nardinebasta/GameofPhones_/ .
items.title_ko: 폰 전쟁: 보이스 피싱 사기에 맞서는 게임 이론 및 LLM 활용
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 게임 이론 프레임워크와 LLM을 활용하여 보이스 피싱 사기에 대응하는 '봇 전쟁'을 제안합니다. 자동화된 에이전트가 사기꾼과 상호 작용하여 사기꾼의 운영 능력을 고갈시키는 전략적 미끼 작전을 펼칩니다.
items.why_ko: AI를 활용하여 실제 사회 문제, 특히 보이스 피싱과 같은 범죄에 능동적으로 대응하는 새로운 접근 방식을 제시하며, AI의 윤리적 활용 사례를 보여줍니다.

items.title: Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility: A Theoretical Framework for Multi-Agent Task Obstructions
items.body: Multi-agent systems can differ under identical agents and communication budgets when they support different forms of joint interaction. We introduce Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility (TSI), a sheaf-theoretic framework separating task-level compatibility obstructions from system capability. A task is represented by an interaction complex $K$ and a capacity sheaf $\mathcal{F}$; nonzero $H^n(K;\mathcal{F})$ defines a structural signature, while registered interventions test capability. For cocycle data, cochain realization is solvable exactly when the represented cohomology class vanishes. Examples show that the signature is sheaf-relative, and the degree-1 reduction yields cycle-space witnesses and observation requirements. We evaluate two finite one-round models. Across 15,625 degree-1 inputs, an all-agent additive primitive solves decision and repair exactly; the optimal pairwise system reaches 88.80% on decision, one input above the 88.79% majority-class baseline, and 26.63% on repair. On a degree-2 tetrahedral-boundary task over 531,441 inputs, the same-2-skeleton system retains all four three-agent primitives yet matches the pairwise-only optimum throughout the registered separation window, whereas adding the class-filling four-agent primitive makes both tasks exact. Status-preserving robustness checks retain exact performance but are not cost-matched to the class-restoring ablation. Conditional on the registered primitives and cost models, TSI provides task-relative, falsifiable tests of higher-order interaction.
items.title_ko: 불가분성의 위상적 시프: 다중 에이전트 태스크 방해에 대한 이론적 프레임워크
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 동일한 에이전트와 통신 예산을 가진 다중 에이전트 시스템이 상이한 형태의 상호 작용을 지원할 때 발생하는 차이점을 다루기 위해 불가분성의 위상적 시프(TSI)라는 시프 이론적 프레임워크를 소개합니다.
items.why_ko: 다중 에이전트 시스템의 복잡한 상호 작용을 이해하고, 태스크 수준의 호환성 문제를 체계적으로 분석하는 데 도움을 주는 이론적 기반을 제공합니다.

items.title: Monsoon: Scalable Spontaneous Speech Collection for Low-Resource ASR in 50 Languages
items.body: For most languages, automatic speech recognition (ASR) is limited less by model architecture than by a lack of accurately transcribed spontaneous speech. We present Monsoon, a framework for collecting such data at scale. It elicits unscripted conversations between paired contributors, screens recordings with automated classifiers, corrects transcripts over five levels of human review, and selects segments for lexical and acoustic coverage. It has collected speech in 50 languages; we analyse seven 3,500-hour corpora. At equal volume, its quality stages reduce semantic word error rate (WER) by 10-39% relative to a conventional protocol. Compared with an architecture-matched baseline trained on public corpora, Whisper fine-tuned on Monsoon performs comparably on the baseline's own test sets and reduces semantic WER by 20-44 points on conversational benchmarks. The gains transfer to a second architecture and grow with data volume. We release the framework, its quality-control models, and the fine-tuned models.
items.title_ko: Monsoon: 50개 언어의 저자원 ASR을 위한 대규모 자발적 음성 수집
items.summary_ko: Monsoon은 50개 언어에 걸쳐 정확하게 전사된 자발적 음성 데이터를 대규모로 수집하기 위한 프레임워크입니다. 이는 저자원 언어의 자동 음성 인식(ASR) 발전을 위한 중요한 데이터셋 구축 프로젝트입니다.
items.why_ko: 대부분의 언어에서 ASR 시스템의 성능이 데이터 부족으로 제한되는 문제를 해결하고, 전 세계 다양한 언어의 AI 접근성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
items.body: Harness development plays a crucial role in building capable AI agents. Recent approaches improve harnesses through recursive self-improvement (RSI), but their performance gains often come with higher execution costs. We introduce HarnessPro, a label-free method for evolving harnesses to improve task performance while reducing execution cost. In this setting, candidate harnesses are evaluated using LLM-generated tests without access to ground-truth solutions or official tests. Specialized agents diagnose execution trajectories, plan updates with different performance-cost priorities, and implement them as candidate harnesses. Rather than returning a single harness, HarnessPro uses normalized weighted squared-distance selection to provide cost-focused (lite), balanced (medium), and performance-focused (heavy) harnesses for different deployment budgets. Selected harnesses enter the next iteration, where execution feedback guides further updates. Our experiments cover Terminal-Bench 2, SWE-Bench Pro, and ProgramBench, using GPT-5.5 with Codex and GLM-5.2 with Claude Code. Across these benchmarks using GPT-5.5 with Codex, the heavy mode of HarnessPro achieves an average pass-rate gain of 2.0 percentage points and an average per-task cost reduction of 26.1% relative to RHO. This advantage also holds when using GLM-5.2 with Claude Code. Code is available at https://github.com/pzs19/HarnessPro
items.title_ko: HarnessPro: 성능-비용 균형을 위한 파레토 최적화 기반 재귀적 하네스 자기 개선
items.summary_ko: HarnessPro는 레이블 없이 하네스를 진화시켜 작업 성능을 향상시키면서 실행 비용을 줄이는 방법론을 제안합니다. 이는 재귀적 자기 개선(RSI) 접근 방식이 성능 향상과 함께 비용 증가를 수반하는 문제를 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트 개발에서 성능과 비용 효율성이라는 두 가지 중요한 목표를 동시에 최적화할 수 있는 실용적인 프레임워크를 제공합니다.

items.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing
items.body: Reinforcement learning enables learning high-performance control policies, but its reliance on extensive interaction limits deployment on physical systems where data collection is costly, and failures are unsafe. We introduce Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA), an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that uses structured simulation priors for rapid adaptation. PIA pretrains a world model on heterogeneous low- and high-fidelity simulated trajectories, then adapts it with limited target-domain interaction using uncertainty-regularized planning. Rather than requiring an accurate simulator for policy transfer, PIA treats simulated trajectories as biased priors whose residual mismatch is corrected during online adaptation. We evaluate PIA in autonomous racing using high-fidelity simulation and on a real full-size autonomous race car. In simulation, PIA adapts faster across track and surface shifts than strong baselines, achieving lower lap times and fewer failures. On hardware, PIA achieves reliable few-shot adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction.
items.title_ko: 자율 주행 경주를 위한 모델 기반 RL의 신속한 적응을 위한 시뮬레이션 사전 지식
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 시뮬레이션 사전 지식을 활용하여 모델 기반 강화 학습(RL)의 신속한 적응을 가능하게 하는 Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA) 프레임워크를 소개합니다. 이는 자율 주행 경주와 같이 데이터 수집이 비싸고 실패가 위험한 실제 시스템에 RL을 배포하는 데 중점을 둡니다.
items.why_ko: 시뮬레이션 데이터를 활용하여 실제 시스템에서의 학습 효율성과 안전성을 크게 향상시키는 방법으로, 자율주행 등 고위험군 AI 시스템 개발에 필수적입니다.

items.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
items.body: Expert human readers process large inputs (e.g., code repositories and long documents) by skimming to closely read only what matters. On the other hand, language models process all input tokens through each model layer, resulting in significant processing costs for long-context inputs. We introduce TokenGate, a small, drop-in component that extends existing trained models to enable end-to-end learnable token pruning over long-context inputs for fast and memory-efficient prefill. To enable end-to-end learning despite the non-differentiable top-K operator for token pruning, we introduce token-gated attention, a mechanism inspired by Mixture-of-Experts that re-weights attention logits using token importance scores. Across diverse tasks, TokenGate achieves $1.4$-$11.3\times$ faster time-to-first token (TTFT) and $1.5$-$3.4\times$ lower peak memory at no accuracy degradation for prefill in transformers. Compared to the best-performing prior methods for token-pruning, TokenGate gives up to $6.4\times$ faster prefill and $2\times$ lower peak memory. TokenGate natively extends both standard transformers (e.g., Qwen3) and hybrid-attention models (e.g., Qwen3.5) with simple lightweight adaptation comparable to standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning. We make our code available at: https://github.com/tokengate-models/TokenGate.
items.body_ko: 전문 인간 독자들은 큰 입력(예: 코드 저장소 및 긴 문서)을 중요한 부분만 자세히 읽기 위해 훑어봅니다. 반면에 언어 모델은 각 모델 레이어를 통해 모든 입력 토큰을 처리하여 긴 컨텍스트 입력에 대해 상당한 처리 비용을 발생시킵니다. 우리는 TokenGate를 소개합니다. TokenGate는 기존 학습된 모델을 확장하여 긴 컨텍스트 입력에 대한 종단 간 학습 가능한 토큰 가지치기를 통해 빠르고 메모리 효율적인 프리필(prefill)을 가능하게 하는 작고 드롭인 가능한 구성 요소입니다. 토큰 가지치기를 위한 미분 불가능한 top-K 연산자에도 불구하고 종단 간 학습을 가능하게 하기 위해, 우리는 Mixture-of-Experts에서 영감을 받아 토큰 중요도 점수를 사용하여 어텐션 로짓에 가중치를 재조정하는 메커니즘인 토큰 게이트 어텐션을 도입합니다. 다양한 작업에서 TokenGate는 트랜스포머의 프리필에서 정확도 저하 없이 1.4-11.3배 더 빠른 TTFT(time-to-first token)와 1.5-3.4배 더 낮은 최고 메모리를 달성합니다. 토큰 가지치기를 위한 최고의 기존 방법과 비교하여 TokenGate는 최대 6.4배 더 빠른 프리필과 2배 더 낮은 최고 메모리를 제공합니다. TokenGate는 표준 트랜스포머(예: Qwen3)와 하이브리드 어텐션 모델(예: Qwen3.5) 모두에 표준 매개변수 효율적인 미세 조정과 유사한 간단하고 가벼운 적응으로 기본적으로 확장됩니다. 코드는 https://github.com/tokengate-models/TokenGate 에서 확인할 수 있습니다.
items.title_ko: TokenGate: 학습된 토큰 가지치기로 LLM의 빠른 프리필 및 메모리 효율성 확보
items.summary_ko: TokenGate는 LLM이 긴 컨텍스트 입력에 대해 빠르고 메모리 효율적인 프리필(prefill)을 수행할 수 있도록 학습된 토큰 가지치기(pruning)를 가능하게 하는 작은 드롭인 컴포넌트입니다. 이는 전체 입력 토큰을 처리하는 기존 LLM의 높은 처리 비용 문제를 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: 긴 컨텍스트를 효율적으로 처리하는 것은 LLM의 실용성을 높이는 데 매우 중요하며, TokenGate는 비용을 절감하면서 성능을 유지하는 새로운 접근 방식을 제시합니다.

items.title: Trajectory Replay: Continuous-Time Mixture Transport for Lifelong Generative Models
items.body: Adapting pre-trained continuous-time generative models to sequentially incoming data without forgetting earlier tasks is a central challenge in lifelong learning. A leading strategy, generative replay, uses a generative model trained on historical tasks to augment its own continual update with synthetic samples from experience. However, it requires full trajectory simulations at every training step, which accumulate discretization errors and can degrade the replayed historical distribution. Here, we propose trajectory replay, which bypasses sample generation by training an updated velocity field to match both a frozen historical velocity along its trajectories and the incoming task's velocity field, weighted by a stability-plasticity coefficient. Through the lens of continuous-time transport, we show the resulting optimum averages the two task velocities by their respective densities and generates the mixture of their probability paths. Combined with mean velocity distillation, trajectory replay accesses historical trajectories using only a few network evaluations per continual update. Empirically, it outperforms generative replay and distillation baselines on class-incremental image generation. In two biological case studies, trajectory replay extends generative perturbation models to new contexts and experimental batches across two data modalities while preserving treatment-effect prediction.
items.title_ko: Trajectory Replay: 평생 생성 모델을 위한 연속 시간 혼합 전송
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 사전 훈련된 연속 시간 생성 모델을 이전 작업을 잊지 않고 순차적으로 들어오는 데이터에 적응시키는 문제를 다룹니다. 기존의 생성적 리플레이 방식의 이산화 오류 및 역사적 분포 저하 문제를 해결하기 위해 '연속 시간 혼합 전송'을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 생성 모델이 새로운 정보를 지속적으로 학습하면서도 이전에 학습한 지식을 보존하는 '평생 학습(lifelong learning)' 능력을 향상시키는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Gradient descent reaches arbitrary accuracy in a fixed number of large steps on multiclass logistic regression
items.body:
We show that gradient descent (GD) with step size $η$ can achieve $\varepsilon$ optimality gap on the multiclass logistic regression loss in a number of iterations $T$ that is independent of $\varepsilon$. To do so, the step size $η$ must be chosen large enough as a function of $\varepsilon$ (and properties of the linearly separable dataset), while $T$ is a constant that only depends on the data. The relevant properties of the data include the number of points and their margin (for $T$), and one additional quantity (for $η$) that turns out to be necessary in dimension $d \geq 3$. The proofs build on the known fact that, as $η\to \infty$, suitably rescaled GD becomes the perceptron algorithm, and the latter finds a perfect classifier in $T$ iterations. A similar claim was shown for two classes in dimension $d = 2$ using other proof techniques.
This result adds to previous works that showed GD on the logistic regression loss can be accelerated by taking large step sizes. Those provoke a wild, oscillatory initial phase, followed by a stable phase. We provide results of this (qualitatively different) nature, too.
items.title_ko: 경사 하강법, 다중 클래스 로지스틱 회귀에서 고정된 스텝 수로 임의의 정확도 달성
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 경사 하강법(GD)이 다중 클래스 로지스틱 회귀 손실에서 $\varepsilon$ 최적성 간격을 달성하는 데 필요한 반복 횟수 $T$가 $\varepsilon$와 무관함을 보여줍니다. 스텝 크기 $\eta$는 $\varepsilon$와 데이터의 선형 분리 가능성에 따라 충분히 크게 선택되어야 합니다.
items.why_ko: 최적화 알고리즘의 수렴 속도에 대한 이론적 이해를 제공하며, 특정 조건에서 경사 하강법의 효율성을 재평가하는 데 중요한 통찰력을 줍니다.

items.title: recAMPLIFY: Large-Scale Pretraining of Recursive Protein Language Models
items.body: Protein language models (pLMs) are powerful tools for protein annotation and mutation-effect prediction, but progress has largely depended on scaling model size and data, making them expensive and prone to memorization. Test-time scaling offers a complementary path, but methods developed for autoregressive LLMs do not transfer directly: masked encoders lack a generation loop, and amino acids do not verbalize in a reasoning language. Instead, we adapt recursive pretraining to masked pLMs, where a weight-tied Transformer core refines residue-aligned hidden states over an adjustable number of cycles. We instantiate this recipe as recAMPLIFY, a pLM with 155M unique parameters trained on the same 2T tokens as AMPLIFY-350M. Despite 56% fewer parameters, it improves CASP contact recovery and three out of four supervised tasks, notably raising fold accuracy by 22.5%. Because optimal depth for recAMPLIFY varies across tasks and assays, we then introduce Gated Mixture Recurrence (GMR), a framework that decodes each protein from a probability-weighted mixture of hidden states visited during recursion. GMR employs a learned residual gate at scalar, low-rank, or per-dimension resolution to control how much of each cycle's proposed update is accepted into the state. This unifies halting and gating into a single adaptive computation objective while recovering PonderNet-style halting as a special case without gates. Layered on top of recAMPLIFY, GMR further reduces expected layer depth by up to 37%, although the accuracy trade-off varies by task. Mechanistic analyses show that residual gating controls recurrence stability beyond the trained depth and that halt depth tracks biological properties.
items.title_ko: recAMPLIFY: 재귀적 단백질 언어 모델의 대규모 사전 훈련
items.summary_ko: recAMPLIFY는 단백질 언어 모델(pLM)의 사전 훈련에 재귀적 사전 훈련 방식을 적용하여, 모델 크기 및 데이터 스케일링에 주로 의존하던 기존 방식의 한계를 극복합니다. 이는 단백질 주석 및 돌연변이 효과 예측에 초점을 맞춥니다.
items.why_ko: 단백질 과학 분야에서 AI 모델의 비용 효율성과 일반화 능력을 향상시키는 새로운 훈련 패러다임을 제시하며, 신약 개발 및 생명 공학 연구에 기여합니다.

items.title: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits
items.body: Muon, a 2024-born optimizer for language models, differs from the 2015-born spectral gradient descent mainly in its fast, GPU-friendly Newton--Schulz polynomial for orthogonalizing the gradient matrix. Accordingly, a line of research proposes faster polynomial iterations for gradient orthogonalization, such as Polar Express and Gram Newton--Schulz, both built on quintic polynomials. In this paper, we introduce Polar Switch, a new approach to polynomial gradient orthogonalization. Using simple polynomial circuits, Polar Switch reaches a given high polynomial degree at a lower FLOP cost than quintic iterations. We define a circuit as a short sequence of symmetric matrix products on a few square buffers, and circuits with $k$ products form a restricted family of odd polynomials of degree up to $2^{k+1}+1$. We choose the sequence of products in each circuit, their coefficients, and how the circuits are composed by numerically minimizing a worst-case bound on the polar approximation error. This minimization is subject to a FLOP budget that accounts for symmetric matrix multiplication kernels and a rounding constraint for numerical stability in half precision. Our two recommended Polar Switch methods have 15.5--18.7\% lower runtime than Polar Express on square matrices and 8.6--16.2\% lower runtime than Gram Newton--Schulz on rectangular matrices with aspect ratios 3.25, 3.5, and 8, with comparable approximation accuracy. In pretraining Modded-NanoGPT \#91, Qwen3-0.6B, and Gemma 3-1B, Polar Switch reaches final validation losses similar to those of established orthogonalization methods. Across the more than 14 million matrices that each of the two recommended methods orthogonalized in these runs, the estimated output spectral norms never exceed the designed bounds by more than 3\%, demonstrating their numerical stability.
items.title_ko: Polar Switch: 다항식 회로를 이용한 빠른 뮤온 직교화
items.summary_ko: Polar Switch는 뮤온(Muon) 최적화기의 핵심인 기울기 행렬 직교화를 위한 새로운 다항식 기울기 직교화 접근 방식을 소개합니다. 기존의 퀸틱 다항식을 기반으로 한 방식보다 단순한 다항식을 사용합니다.
items.why_ko: 언어 모델 최적화에 사용되는 기울기 직교화의 효율성을 개선하여, 대규모 모델 학습 속도와 안정성을 향상시키는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: CAVA: Complementary-Label-Aware Data Valuation
items.body: Complementary-label learning (CLL) trains a classifier from labels that name a class an instance does not belong to. Such labels are cheap to collect from crowdworkers or vision-language models (VLMs), making them attractive for large-scale annotation. However, both sources can mistakenly assign the true class as the complementary label. Such annotation errors are particularly harmful in CLL because the model is explicitly trained to suppress the correct answer. Optimal transport (OT) data valuation identifies harmful samples by comparing training data with a clean validation set, but transferring it directly to CLL creates a semantic mismatch: label $c$ means not class $c$ in the training but class $c$ in the validation. We show that this makes the OT label groups noisy mixtures whose behavior depends on the noise rate. The transferred score is informative only at sufficiently high noise, becomes uninformative at the crossover rate $1/M$ for $M$ classes, and reverses below it, where practical CLL annotation typically operates. We propose CAVA, which introduces a complementary label cost and a label margin that isolates the contribution of each complementary label to the transport potential. The margin keeps a consistent direction across noise rates, detects diagonal noise with a parameter-free threshold of closed-form precision, and allows detected samples to be recycled as ordinary-label supervision. On synthetic and human-annotated benchmarks, CAVA separates diagonal noise almost perfectly where directly transferred OT valuation performs worse than random. With only a fraction of the clean validation data, it also improves every CLL objective we evaluate, showing that OT-based valuation becomes reliable once the semantics of complementary supervision are modeled explicitly.
items.title_ko: CAVA: 보완 레이블 인식 데이터 가치 평가
items.summary_ko: CAVA(Complementary-Label-Aware Data Valuation)는 보완 레이블 학습(CLL)에서 발생할 수 있는 레이블 오류의 해로움을 해결하기 위해 최적 운송(OT) 데이터 가치 평가를 사용합니다. 이는 크라우드워커나 VLM으로부터 얻은 보완 레이블의 신뢰성을 높입니다.
items.why_ko: 비용 효율적인 데이터 수집 방식인 보완 레이블 학습의 신뢰성을 높여, 대규모 데이터셋 구축 및 AI 모델 훈련의 효율성을 개선합니다.

items.title: Cross-Fitting for Neural Posterior Estimation
items.body: Neural Posterior Estimation (NPE) fits an amortized conditional density estimator to a simulated training set of complete-data realizations. NPE's training objective, log-likelihood, favors posterior approximations that assign arbitrarily high density to the training points, and typical families of amortized conditional density estimators (e.g., normalizing flows, Gaussian encoders) are flexible enough to oblige. The resulting policy of extreme overconfidence translates poorly to held-out data. Early stopping and other regularizers can prevent this degeneracy, but they are limited to selecting posterior approximations along an unfavorable optimization trajectory set by in-sample residuals, where the posterior mean is underfit while the posterior variance is overfit. To avoid this trade-off, we propose Cross-Fitting NPE (CF-NPE), which uses sample splitting to separate conditional-mean estimation from the estimation of the posterior's higher moments. Using $K$-fold cross-fitting, CF-NPE fits $K$ posterior-mean regressors and then fits a conditional density estimator to the resulting out-of-fold residuals. In experiments with synthetic data and in a cosmological application, CF-NPE achieves higher held-out log-likelihood than standard NPE and typically improves calibration. CF-NPE is most useful in high-dimensional, simulation-limited settings.
items.title_ko: 신경 사후 추정을 위한 교차 검증 (Cross-Fitting)
items.summary_ko: 신경 사후 추정(NPE)이 훈련 데이터에 지나치게 높은 밀도를 할당하여 새로운 데이터에 대한 일반화가 잘 되지 않는 문제를 해결하기 위해 '교차 검증(Cross-Fitting)'을 제안합니다. 이는 과도한 자신감 정책으로 인한 성능 저하를 방지합니다.
items.why_ko: 베이즈 추론의 핵심인 사후 분포 추정의 정확성과 일반화 능력을 향상시켜, 불확실성 모델링 및 결정 과학 분야의 AI 적용에 기여합니다.

items.title: EpiLens: Lightweight RAG for Epidemiological Knowledge Acquisition
items.body: To prepare for future outbreaks, researchers need to know what studies have been done and what data they use. Mapping a large literature by hand is slow, while large language models alone can misstate or conflate sources. We present EpiLens, a lightweight, open-source retrieval-augmented generation package that applies a fixed retrieval template and output schema to every paper in a corpus and links outputs to source passages. We build a corpus of 2,297 papers from the sources of a multi-pathogen parameter study and evaluate EpiLens's paper-classification workflow against 214 manually labelled papers. Without task-specific training data, the classifier matches or exceeds the tested supervised and zero-shot baselines across four tasks. The study's early extraction sheets cite published sources for 327 estimates. We link each estimate to a cited document or to corpus studies included by a review. Then, we use the classifier's labels to compare the papers associated with different parameters and pathogens. EpiLens labels more papers linked to reproduction numbers than fatality risks as model-based (54% versus 22%, compared with 62% versus 24% in the manual labels). The gap is consistent with the frequent use of transmission models to estimate reproduction numbers and persists within each of five pathogens compared. Beyond the contrast between parameters, the model-based share of papers linked to incubation-period estimates differs by pathogen: 55% for SARS-CoV-2 versus 6% for mpox.
items.title_ko: EpiLens: 역학 지식 습득을 위한 경량 RAG
items.summary_ko: EpiLens는 역학적 지식 습득을 위한 경량 오픈소스 검색 증강 생성(RAG) 패키지입니다. 이는 대규모 문헌 매핑을 수동으로 하거나 LLM 단독 사용 시 발생하는 오류 문제를 해결하고, 출력과 원문을 연결합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 한계인 환각(hallucination) 문제를 해결하고, 특정 도메인에서 정확하고 신뢰할 수 있는 정보를 제공하는 RAG 시스템의 중요성을 강조합니다.

items.title: Injection of Space Radiation Errors on Low-power NVM using Generative Deep Learning
items.body: We develop an error model for a Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) device that represents the effects of physical faults experienced in a CubeSat mission in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). The CubeSat carries an off-the-shelf low-power Ferroelectric RAM (FRAM) chip and runs repeated read/write tests according to a predefined pattern. We compare every memory snapshot received from the satellite with a reference bitmap to identify bit errors. We visually analyze erroneous values distributions in the memory snapshots and we understand that they are frequently distributed according to regular spatial patterns. We define a generative deep learning technique to automatically learn these spatial patterns and to synthetically generate additional error patterns mimicking the observed ones. The model is capable at producing memory errors for general application-level experimentation. Our preliminary validation indicates that when comparing the model output with the data we collect, 0.92 of the generated bit flips correspond to bit flips in the memory snapshots and the model captures 0.91 of the observed bit flips. A comparison of the spatial distribution of bit flips in 10,000 generated error patterns also provides a Wasserstein distance of 0.073, indicating that the two distributions differ by roughly 7% of the maximum possible displacement of their probability masses.
items.title_ko: 생성형 딥러닝을 이용한 저전력 비휘발성 메모리의 우주 방사선 오류 주입
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 큐브위성 임무에서 저전력 강유전체 RAM(FRAM) 칩에 발생하는 물리적 결함의 영향을 나타내는 오류 모델을 개발합니다. 생성형 딥러닝을 사용하여 메모리 스냅샷의 오류 값 분포를 시각적으로 분석합니다.
items.why_ko: 우주 환경에서의 AI 시스템 안정성 및 신뢰성 확보에 중요한 연구로, 극한 환경에서 사용되는 AI 하드웨어 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: Copying Under Repetition: From Prefix Matching to Position Hashing
items.body: Frontier LLMs can copy random text almost flawlessly, yet they often overrun or truncate long blocks of repeated characters. In repeated strings, matching local content no longer reliably identifies where copying should continue or when it should stop. Nevertheless, we show that a two-layer transformer with $O(\log\log N)$-bit precision and $O(\log N/\log\log N)$ width can copy every string up to a chosen design horizon $N$ and terminate correctly under arbitrary repetition. We use RoPE-style rotations of attention values and outputs (VO-rotations) with small prime periods to encode distances from delimiter anchors modulo those primes. By the Chinese Remainder Theorem, these periodic encodings jointly distinguish all required distances, allowing one retrieval rule to select either the next source token or the end marker. In contrast, we prove a width-independent impossibility result for copying under sequential finite-precision softmax accumulation. It applies to transformers whose only positional input is an additive attention bias that eventually becomes constant, including NoPE and a recursive implementation of ALiBi. Once an identical-token run exceeds the resulting saturation threshold, further repetitions leave the logits unchanged. If this threshold grows sublinearly with $N$, these models cannot both complete a long all-identical copy and stop correctly, a pattern resembling the termination errors of frontier LLMs. In synthetic copying experiments, baseline transformer models fail on long repeated strings even within the training range. Trained VO models, by contrast, generalize beyond the training lengths with near-perfect accuracy up to length $\approx 5005$, the selected primes' period product.
items.title_ko: 반복 시 복사: 접두사 일치에서 위치 해싱으로
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 최신 LLM이 무작위 텍스트는 거의 완벽하게 복사하지만, 반복되는 긴 문자 블록에서 오버런 또는 잘림 현상이 발생하는 문제를 다룹니다. $O(\log\log N)$-비트 정밀도와 $O(\log N/\log\log N)$ 너비의 2계층 트랜스포머가 임의의 반복에서도 모든 문자열을 올바르게 복사하고 종료할 수 있음을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 긴 반복 패턴을 포함한 텍스트를 처리하는 방식의 한계를 이해하고, 이를 극복할 수 있는 새로운 아키텍처를 제시하여 LLM의 견고성을 높입니다.

items.title: Deep Pontryagin Learning for Continuous-Time Stochastic Control with Jumps
items.body: We develop a deep Pontryagin learning framework for high-dimensional continuous-time stochastic control problems that naturally accommodates jump-diffusions. In contrast to direct policy optimization, which repeatedly differentiates the objective through the entire time-discretized dynamics, our method separates adjoint learning from policy improvement by explicitly incorporating state-sensitivity information from the Pontryagin stochastic maximum principle. For a fixed Markov control, we first compute pathwise adjoint labels by backpropagating the reward through time along simulated state trajectories, and project these labels onto the Markov state through a supervised regression step. The control is then updated by enforcing the pointwise Hamiltonian stationarity condition. We prove that the resulting projected adjoint process satisfies a discrete-time Pontryagin principle and converges, as the time step tends to zero, to the solution of the corresponding continuous-time adjoint backward stochastic differential equation. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy, stability, and scalability of the approach.
items.title_ko: 점프를 동반한 연속 시간 확률 제어를 위한 딥 폰트랴긴 학습
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 고차원 연속 시간 확률 제어 문제를 위한 딥 폰트랴긴 학습 프레임워크를 개발합니다. 이는 정책 개선과 수반 학습을 분리하여 상태 민감도 정보를 명시적으로 통합함으로써 점프 확산을 자연스럽게 수용합니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 동적 시스템의 제어 문제를 해결하는 데 새로운 접근 방식을 제시하며, 금융, 로봇 공학 등 다양한 분야의 AI 제어 시스템 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: HoloCosm: Beyond Single-Metric Benchmark Compression Across Multiple Metrics
items.body: Benchmark compression reduces evaluation cost by selecting a small set of samples. Existing methods typically guide selection using a single metric, although benchmarks often assess models along multiple dimensions. We find that model rankings are often weakly correlated across metrics, indicating that different metrics capture distinct aspects of model performance. Samples selected for one metric do not reliably preserve scores and rankings on others when used for compressed evaluation. At 80\% compression, each of the five single-metric baselines yields higher reconstruction error than equal-size random sampling in over 70\% of cross-metric comparisons. To address this challenge, we present HoloCosm, which jointly minimizes normalized score-reconstruction error across source models and metrics while constraining ranking distortion. We evaluate HoloCosm across multiple compression rates on 15 language, multimodal, VLA, and agent benchmark configurations with 85 component metrics. With 80\% compression, HoloCosm outperforms Random, the strongest baseline overall: average NMAE drops by 35.3\% to 0.236, worst-component NMAE drops by 39.5\% to 0.330, and average Spearman correlation rises from 0.884 to 0.915. In addition, HoloCosm remains competitive with existing baselines in single-metric evaluation. We will release our code and experimental results.
items.title_ko: HoloCosm: 단일 메트릭을 넘어 여러 메트릭에 걸친 벤치마크 압축
items.summary_ko: HoloCosm은 벤치마크 압축에서 단일 메트릭을 넘어 여러 메트릭에 걸쳐 샘플을 선택하는 방법을 제시합니다. 기존 방법이 단일 메트릭에 치중하여 모델 순위가 메트릭마다 약하게 상관관계가 있음을 발견하고, 이를 해결하여 다차원적인 모델 성능 평가를 가능하게 합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델의 성능을 다각적으로 평가하고 벤치마크 비용을 효율적으로 관리하는 데 중요한 방법론으로, 종합적인 모델 선택 및 최적화에 기여합니다.

items.title: Doubly Robust Learning of Heterogeneous Survival Treatment Effects under Time-Varying Treatments
items.body: Estimating heterogeneous survival treatment effects (HSTEs) from time-to-event data under time-varying treatments is important in fields such as medicine (e.g., to decide which sequence of treatments is better in terms of survival probability). However, this task is challenging because treatment decisions, patient characteristics, and censoring probability often evolve together, requiring sequential adjustment for both treatments and censoring. Existing survival learners mostly consider a single baseline treatment assignment, while longitudinal treatment-effect learners typically assume uncensored outcomes. In this paper, we introduce a novel doubly robust learner for heterogeneous survival treatment effects under time-varying treatments and history-dependent censoring. Our framework separates the intervention window from the survival horizon, with treatment prescribed for a finite period, after which care follows its natural course. We further establish the favorable theoretical properties of Neyman-orthogonality, rate double robustness and quasi-oracle efficiency. The framework accommodates flexible machine learning models for nuisance estimation and treatment-effect regression. We evaluate our learners through several numerical experiments, demonstrating their effectiveness.
items.title_ko: 시간 변화 치료 하의 이질적인 생존 치료 효과에 대한 이중 강건 학습
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 시간 변화 치료 하에서 이질적인 생존 치료 효과(HSTE)를 추정하는 이중 강건 학습 방법을 제시합니다. 이는 치료 결정, 환자 특성 및 검열 확률이 함께 진화하는 복잡한 문제를 해결하는 데 중점을 둡니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 분야에서 개인 맞춤형 치료 전략을 개발하는 데 필수적인 방법론으로, AI가 복잡한 시계열 의료 데이터를 분석하는 능력을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: GeoSplit: Selective Edge--Server Map Acquisition for Cross-User Travel-Mode Recognition
items.body: Networked mobility sensing couples local trajectory inference with remote geospatial context, making communication decisions part of the prediction system. We present GeoSplit, an edge--server framework for travel-mode recognition that separates the utility of map evidence, its training-time transfer, and its selective acquisition at runtime. On GeoLife with 10% labels, we evaluate these components under user-day and user-disjoint grouping. For unseen users, aligned full-map context raises macro-F1 from 0.7154 to 0.7864, while map-informed distillation yields a motion-only student at 0.7225. Through a compact query interface, entropy gating achieves 0.7729 macro-F1 versus 0.7738 for all queries, querying 39.5% of trajectories and reducing application payload by 60.5%. Under user-day grouping, selective and all-query scores are similarly close at a 21.6% query rate. Learned value estimation and probability fusion offer no consistent improvement. These results illustrate communication-efficient edge--server inference for an intelligent transportation sensing task.
items.title_ko: GeoSplit: 사용자 간 이동 모드 인식을 위한 선택적 에지-서버 지도 획득
items.summary_ko: GeoSplit은 에지-서버 프레임워크로, 이동 모드 인식을 위해 지도 증거의 유틸리티, 훈련 시간 전송, 런타임 시 선택적 획득을 분리합니다. 이는 로컬 궤적 추론과 원격 지리 공간 컨텍스트를 결합하여 통신 결정을 최적화합니다.
items.why_ko: 에지 컴퓨팅 환경에서 AI 모델의 효율적인 배포와 데이터 통신 최적화를 통해, 모바일 기기에서의 위치 기반 서비스 및 스마트 모빌리티 솔루션 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: Towards Robust Model Organisms for Eliciting Latent Knowledge
items.body:
A key problem in AI safety is eliciting latent knowledge (ELK), extracting information from a model that is misaligned and more knowledgeable than its overseer. For example, a misaligned model used to scan code for vulnerabilities may want to withhold its findings, i.e., sandbag, in order to exploit them later. To study ELK empirically, we need model organisms that mirror this setting. Existing model organisms fall short in several respects. In this work, we train model organisms to withhold solutions in a vulnerability detection task. We combine transcript distillation with counter-prompting and tamper-resistance training to instill three properties that we argue are critical for a useful ELK testbed: 1) Selectivity, the model sandbags when it thinks the overseer doesn't know the answer and complies otherwise, 2) Robustness, the model resists elicitation, and 3) Retention, the model retains a knowledge advantage over the overseer, as opposed to losing the relevant capability. We train a sequence of model organisms and show that our strongest model substantially outperforms prior models on robustness while keeping the other two properties intact. We hope that our model organisms provide a useful ELK testbed for the community, and that our methodology sparks the development of increasingly challenging model organisms.
All our code, models and the dataset are available at https://huggingface.co/collections/lennart-finke/sandbagging.
items.title_ko: 잠재 지식 유도를 위한 강건한 모델 유기체 개발
items.summary_ko: AI 안전의 핵심 문제인 잠재 지식 유도(ELK)를 연구하기 위해, 연구자들은 실제 환경을 모방한 '모델 유기체'를 훈련합니다. 이는 모델이 잘못 정렬되어 감시자보다 더 많은 지식을 가지고 있을 때 정보를 추출하는 것을 목표로 합니다.
items.why_ko: AI의 잠재적 위험(예: 샌드배깅)을 탐지하고 관리하는 데 중요한 연구로, 안전하고 투명한 AI 시스템 구축을 위한 근본적인 해결책을 모색합니다.

items.title: Hierarchical Token Merging with Recursive Autoencoders for Unsupervised Grammar Induction
items.body: Hierarchical abstraction is a fundamental principle across many data modalities, enabling complex sequences to be represented compositionally at multiple levels. Learning such hierarchies directly from data, without explicit structural supervision, remains a central challenge in representation learning. We investigate whether meaningful hierarchical structure can emerge from compression alone. While autoencoders learn compressed representations through reconstruction, this objective does not necessarily favour meaningful compositional structure. We study this challenge through unsupervised grammar induction, where the underlying hierarchy can be evaluated explicitly. We introduce a hierarchical token-merging autoencoder that recursively combines adjacent tokens into increasingly abstract representations, compressing entire sequences through a variational information bottleneck. The model jointly learns representations and hierarchical structure by marginalising over possible binary trees using dynamic programming. To address training instability, we combine independently trained models through unsupervised consensus and distillation. Experiments on a synthetic, ambiguous grammar demonstrate the emergence of meaningful hierarchical structure without structural supervision. The resulting model achieves 93% grammatical parse-validity and 93% exact reconstruction on held-out sequences, compared with 42% parse-validity for the strongest trivial baseline. These findings establish a proof of concept for hierarchical token merging as a mechanism for unsupervised structure discovery and abstraction learning.
items.title_ko: 계층적 자동 인코더를 이용한 비지도 문법 유도를 위한 계층적 토큰 병합
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 비지도 문법 유도를 위해 재귀적 자동 인코더와 계층적 토큰 병합을 제안합니다. 이는 복잡한 시퀀스를 여러 수준에서 구성적으로 표현할 수 있도록 데이터로부터 계층적 구조를 직접 학습하는 방법을 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 데이터에서 의미 있는 계층적 구조를 자동으로 추출하는 능력은 언어 이해, 이미지 인식 등 다양한 AI 분야에서 심층 학습 모델의 성능을 향상시키는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Parallel Language Models via Variational Decoding
items.body: Autoregressive language models emit one token per forward pass. This causes high inference latency, in particular as models are scaled up for quality. In this paper, we introduce Parallel Language Models (PLMs), which generate mutually consistent tokens in one forward pass by routing dependencies through latent auxiliary variables. PLMs are trained using a variational bound that reduces to an autoregressive loss plus a parallel decoding loss. Empirically, PLMs are on a faster and better Pareto frontier than autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines. Pretrained PLMs achieve near-autoregressive pretraining loss on model scales of 80M to 3B parameters, and speedup follows a power law in model size. When post-trained, our 1.3B model matches or exceeds an identically trained autoregressive model on math, coding, and instruction-following benchmarks, speeding up inference $2.3\text{-}5.7\times$. Together, we show that parallel generation can be trained from a single training objective at autoregressive quality. We will make our code available at https://github.com/mandt-lab/plm.
items.title_ko: 변이형 디코딩을 통한 병렬 언어 모델
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 자기회귀 언어 모델의 높은 추론 지연 시간을 해결하기 위해, 잠재 보조 변수를 통해 종속성을 라우팅하여 상호 일관된 토큰을 한 번의 순방향 패스로 생성하는 병렬 언어 모델(PLM)을 소개합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 추론 속도를 혁신적으로 개선하여 실시간 응답이 필요한 AI 애플리케이션의 개발을 가속화하고, 사용자 경험을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: Mitigating Rubric Hacking through Latent Dimension Recovery and Balancing
items.body: Rubric hacking limits both performance and training robustness in rubric-based reinforcement learning. By decomposing rubrics into sub-dimensions, we reveal the Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: as the total rubric score increases, certain sub-dimension scores systematically decrease, suggesting the model sacrifices specific quality aspects to optimize the aggregated objective. From the sub-dimension perspective, we observe two phenomena: (1) dimension imbalance, causing the policy to favor heavily covered dimensions; (2) dimension absence, leading to a systematic gap between rewards and true quality. To mitigate these issues, we propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation (FRDA), which has generations compete within each dimension separately to mitigate rubric imbalance, and Residual Semantic Dimension Completion (RSDC), which mines evaluation dimensions implicitly encoded in a holistic preference signal to complete rubric coverage. Experiments in chat, science, and medical domains indicate that FRDA mitigates rubric hacking with more stable improvements, while RSDC outperforms both single-reward training and naive multi-reward aggregation, yielding generally higher-quality responses.
items.title_ko: 내부 루브릭 보상 발산: 잠재 차원 복구 및 균형을 통한 루브릭 해킹 완화
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 루브릭 기반 강화 학습에서 '루브릭 해킹'이 성능과 훈련 견고성을 저해하는 문제를 다룹니다. 루브릭을 하위 차원으로 분해하여 특정 하위 차원 점수가 체계적으로 감소하는 '내부 루브릭 보상 발산' 현상을 밝혀냅니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 단일 목표에 편향되지 않고 복합적인 목표를 균형 있게 달성하도록 돕는 중요한 연구로, AI 시스템의 견고성과 공정성을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: StepBench: Diagnosing Real-World Procedural Understanding in AI Agents
items.body: Evaluating an agent's planning ability remains challenging for open-domain tasks, where verifying procedures through execution is often impractical. Existing evaluations typically assess only the final plan and do not distinguish procedural errors such as missing, incorrect, or misordered actions. We introduce STEPBENCH, a benchmark of 6,885 verified procedures crawled from wikiHow across 81 open-domain categories. From each procedure, we derive 5 diagnostic tasks: four with deterministic answers involving withheld, incorrect, or shuffled steps, and one requiring next-step generation. We additionally evaluate full-plan generation to examine how diagnostic performance correlates with end-to-end plan validity. Using the same procedures across tasks lets us directly compare different planning capabilities. For generation, STEPEVAL identifies critical failures that prevent goal completion. Across 14 configurations of 12 models, we find substantial differences across planning capabilities, with step ordering proving the most difficult: the strongest model correctly orders only 63.0% of procedures, dropping to 33.1% for those with nine or more steps. Incorrect-step detection also predicts judged plan validity across models, suggesting a lower-cost alternative for evaluating generation quality.
