On STEPBENCH-Val, comprising 214 procedures published in 2026, comprehension scores and rankings remain stable, suggesting limited influence from memorisation.
items.title_ko: StepBench: AI 에이전트의 실제 절차적 이해 진단
items.summary_ko: STEPBENCH는 AI 에이전트의 계획 능력을 평가하는 새로운 벤치마크로, wikiHow에서 수집한 6,885개의 검증된 절차를 기반으로 합니다. 이 벤치마크는 최종 계획뿐만 아니라 누락, 부정확하거나 잘못된 순서의 행동과 같은 절차적 오류를 진단합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 복잡한 다단계 작업을 실제 환경에서 얼마나 잘 이해하고 수행하는지 평가하는 데 필수적인 도구로, 더욱 스마트한 AI 에이전트 개발을 촉진합니다.

items.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows
items.body: LLM agentic workflows increasingly employ different models for specialized roles. Users may prefer different trade-offs between task quality and deployment cost, sometimes also considering latency. Finding good assignments incurs a separate search cost from evaluating multiple candidates. We introduce Cost-Coupled Gittins (CC-Gittins), a multi-objective extension of single-objective cost-aware Gittins search for Pareto recommendation. It exploits the coupling between evaluation and deployment costs: assignments that cost more to deploy also cost more to evaluate. The search alternates between seeking higher quality and lower deployment cost, reusing each evaluation to inform both searches. After each batch, CC-Gittins recommends assignments that are nondominated under uncertainty-adjusted estimates of quality and deployment cost. We evaluate CC-Gittins on eight quality--cost matrices from workflows with two to five roles and up to 1,681 candidate assignments. We also evaluate the method with latency as a third objective. Across the eight benchmarks, CC-Gittins recovers a substantial fraction of the true Pareto frontier at roughly 10% of the exhaustive-evaluation cost, and recovers most of the frontier with few false positives by 30%.
items.title_ko: 어떤 역할에 어떤 모델? LLM 에이전트 워크플로우를 위한 비용 효율적인 파레토 추천
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 LLM 에이전트 워크플로우에서 특정 역할에 가장 적합한 모델을 비용 효율적으로 추천하는 '비용 결합 기틴스(CC-Gittins)' 방법을 제안합니다. 이는 작업 품질과 배포 비용 간의 다양한 절충점을 고려합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트 시스템을 구축할 때 여러 모델의 성능과 비용을 최적화하여, 실제 서비스 환경에서 AI 솔루션의 경제성과 효율성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: PACT: Plan-Augmented Coordination via Trace-Graphs for Dynamic Multi-Agent Combinatorial Optimization
items.body: Multi-agent approaches have been investigated recently as a means of improving the scalability of reinforcement learning for neural combinatorial optimization. Existing methods assume that all problem instance information is known upfront. However, real-world problems are often dynamic: relevant information is progressively revealed as the agents take actions (e.g., arriving at an edge in a routing problem only to discover it is untraversable). In such cases, existing methods fail to coordinate agents to explore and exploit the progressively revealed information. To address the arising coordination challenge, we introduce PACT (Plan-Augmented Coordination via Trace-graphs). PACT augments the environment graph with auxiliary nodes representing the plans of agents, which are connected to the resource nodes to indicate future dependencies. The proposed message-passing scheme over the augmented graph grounds inter-agent coordination in the environment and enables proactive, rather than reactive, conflict resolution. We show that PACT improves solution quality in dynamic problems relative to baselines and exhibits the best transfer to larger instances on which, remarkably, it outperforms centralized oracles with privileged access to instance uncertainty.
items.title_ko: PACT: 동적 다중 에이전트 조합 최적화를 위한 플랜 증강 조정을 통한 트레이스 그래프
items.summary_ko: PACT는 동적 다중 에이전트 조합 최적화 문제를 해결하기 위해 계획 증강 조정을 트레이스 그래프를 통해 제공합니다. 이는 문제 인스턴스 정보가 미리 알려져 있다고 가정하는 기존 방법의 한계를 극복하고, 에이전트가 행동하면서 관련 정보가 점진적으로 드러나는 상황에 적응합니다.
items.why_ko: 실시간으로 변화하는 환경에서 다중 에이전트 시스템이 효율적으로 협력하고 최적의 결정을 내리도록 돕는 중요한 기술로, 물류, 자원 관리 등 동적 환경에서의 AI 적용에 유용합니다.

items.title: Nested Shared-Operator Recursion on ARC-AGI-1: An Empirical Study of HRM, TRM and URM
items.body: Recursive reasoning models refine persistent internal states by repeatedly applying learned operators. We investigate whether adding a persistent intermediate state that integrates repeated updates of a faster state through the same operator improves predictive performance relative to each model family's baseline at matched parameter counts. We define this organisation operationally and implement it within three architectures: the Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM), Tiny Recursive Model (TRM) and Universal Reasoning Model (URM). Using the official codebases on ARC-AGI-1, we compare each baseline with its parameter-matched nested variant. We evaluate held-out queries from tasks whose demonstrations were available during training. The experiments use a single-GPU budget far below the published training protocols. Under the tested conditions, nested variants show no consistent advantage in token accuracy, predictive loss or exact solving, which remains near zero for all configurations. The results therefore leave the hypothesis open. We specify a confirmatory comparison, with an informative baseline, multiple seeds, controls that isolate nesting and predefined criteria, to determine whether this organisation merits further development.
items.title_ko: ARC-AGI-1에 대한 중첩된 공유-연산자 재귀: HRM, TRM, URM의 실증 연구
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 재귀적 추론 모델이 학습된 연산자를 반복적으로 적용하여 지속적인 내부 상태를 개선하는 방법을 탐구합니다. 특히 Hierarchical Reasoning Model(HRM), Tiny Recursive Model(TRM), Universal Recursive Model(URM) 세 가지 아키텍처 내에서 중첩된 공유-연산자 재귀의 효과를 실증적으로 조사합니다.
items.why_ko: 재귀적 추론 모델의 내부 작동 방식과 성능 개선 가능성을 탐구하여, 복잡한 문제 해결을 위한 AI 모델 아키텍처 설계에 중요한 통찰력을 제공합니다.

items.title: Honeypots for AI Agent Insider Threats
items.body: AI agents deployed inside organizations can pose an insider threat if they make mistakes, are compromised by an attacker, or pursue misaligned objectives. We propose honeypots as an AI control method to improve the security of internal agent deployments. Rather than only using honeypots for pre-deployment evaluations, defenders should plant decoy opportunities for harmful actions throughout the production environment to detect misbehavior, incriminate malicious agents, and deter attacks. Such honeypots can elicit misbehavior under real deployment conditions, identify malicious agents even if chain-of-thought monitorability degrades, provide reliable warnings about agent misbehavior to security teams, and scale cheaply to many agent instances. The presence of honeypots also introduces uncertainty about which opportunities are real, thus deterring malicious agents from attacking and reducing the rate of misbehavior. We discuss the limitations of honeypots and give reasons to expect them to remain effective as agent capabilities increase. Finally, we outline key research questions to measure and improve the effectiveness of honeypots: testing the robustness of honeypots, comparing their detection effectiveness with other monitoring methods, understanding their incrimination and deterrence effects, and building supporting infrastructure.
items.body_ko: 조직 내에 배포된 AI 에이전트는 실수를 저지르거나, 공격자에 의해 침해되거나, 잘못 정렬된 목표를 추구할 경우 내부자 위협을 초래할 수 있습니다. 우리는 내부 에이전트 배포의 보안을 향상시키기 위한 AI 제어 방법으로 허니팟을 제안합니다. 배포 전 평가에만 허니팟을 사용하는 대신, 방어자는 잘못된 행동을 감지하고, 악의적인 에이전트를 고발하며, 공격을 저지하기 위해 전체 프로덕션 환경에 유해한 행동에 대한 미끼 기회를 심어야 합니다. 이러한 허니팟은 실제 배포 조건에서 잘못된 행동을 유도하고, 사고 과정 모니터링 기능이 저하되더라도 악의적인 에이전트를 식별하며, 보안 팀에 에이전트의 잘못된 행동에 대한 신뢰할 수 있는 경고를 제공하고, 많은 에이전트 인스턴스에 저렴하게 확장될 수 있습니다. 허니팟의 존재는 또한 어떤 기회가 실제인지에 대한 불확실성을 유발하여 악의적인 에이전트가 공격하는 것을 저지하고 잘못된 행동의 비율을 줄입니다. 우리는 허니팟의 한계에 대해 논의하고 에이전트 기능이 증가함에 따라 허니팟이 계속 효과적일 것이라고 예상하는 이유를 제시합니다. 마지막으로, 허니팟의 효과를 측정하고 개선하기 위한 주요 연구 질문을 제시합니다: 허니팟의 견고성 테스트, 다른 모니터링 방법과의 탐지 효율성 비교, 고발 및 억제 효과 이해, 지원 인프라 구축.
items.title_ko: AI 에이전트 내부자 위협에 대한 허니팟
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 AI 에이전트가 실수하거나 공격자에게 침해당하거나 잘못 정렬된 목표를 추구할 경우 발생할 수 있는 내부자 위협에 대응하기 위해 '허니팟'을 AI 제어 방법으로 제안합니다. 이는 배포 후 환경에서도 오작동을 탐지하고 공격을 저지하는 데 사용됩니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트의 보안과 신뢰성을 확보하기 위한 새로운 방어 메커니즘을 제시하며, AI 시스템 배포 시 발생할 수 있는 잠재적 위험에 대한 선제적 대응을 가능하게 합니다.

items.title: AllPath: Layered Verification for a Deployed, Self-Revising LLM Trading Agent under Human-Gated and Autonomous Regimes
items.body: LLM trading agents are evaluated almost exclusively in backtests and autonomous benchmark harnesses. Deployment, where actions are irreversible, raises a different question: who verifies the agent's actions, and which failures can each verifier structurally catch? We report on AllPath, a personal LLM trading agent deployed against a live paper-brokerage account. The system watches positions through a deterministic rules engine, and each night it reviews its own day and proposes revisions to its own trading strategies. Verification is split across three layers. Code verifies what must not depend on judgment: deterministic gates enforce risk limits and block any strategy revision that fails an integrity check. The agent verifies itself within fixed bounds: its nightly review has an iteration cap and no tools that can act. A human verifies judgment, through approval screens that show the current state of each proposal. We also compared two verification policies for the agent's self-revisions on the live system: two and a half weeks with every self-revision human-gated, then five weeks with reflection revisions auto-applied behind the same code gates, while the operator's chat channel stayed human-gated throughout. Each layer caught a different kind of failure. The code gates rejected no proposal; their role was keeping revisions consistent. The human rejected two proposals that passed every code check, both over a disagreement about the market, and later removed 11 of the 19 rules the agent had added on its own, at a median lag of eight days. The most instructive production incidents, such as strategies silently left unmonitored, passed every gate; the operator found them by hand, and the fix each time was an interface change that makes the condition visible. We contribute the layered architecture, the two-regime account, and a production incident taxonomy, none observable in a backtest.
items.title_ko: AllPath: 인간 개입 및 자율 모드 하의 배포된 자기 수정 LLM 트레이딩 에이전트를 위한 계층적 검증
items.summary_ko: AllPath는 실제 종이 계좌에 배포된 개인 LLM 트레이딩 에이전트로, 에이전트의 행동을 검증하고 실패를 구조적으로 포착하는 계층적 검증 방법을 보고합니다. 에이전트는 매일 자체 행동을 검토하고 수정 사항을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 트레이딩 에이전트의 실제 배포 및 운영 시 발생할 수 있는 위험을 관리하고, 자율성과 인간 감독 사이의 균형을 찾는 실용적인 접근 방식을 제시합니다.

items.title: Tandem: Serving Hybrid Linear-Attention GUI Agents on Mobile NPUs
items.body: Smartphone GUI agents complete tasks in mobile apps by repeatedly reading the screen and asking a model for the next action. Mobile neural processing units (NPUs) enable local execution, keeping screen contents on the phone, but model latency accumulates with every action. Hybrid linear attention models reduce memory requirements, yet reusing their recurrent state requires checkpoints at the appropriate input positions. Agent requests retain instructions but rewrite recent history, so checkpoint policies designed for chat continuation can miss reusable prefixes. Retaining rollback states for speculative decoding can also move prompt processing off the NPU's matrix unit, adding overhead that outweighs decoding savings on short action outputs. A loaded model can further hold the NPU awake between tasks. We present Tandem, a runtime for hybrid GUI agents on mobile NPUs. Tandem saves recurrent state where consecutive prompts diverge, allowing later requests to reuse previously processed context. It keeps most prefill on the matrix unit and produces rollback states through a short per-token tail. Its verification kernel reads each weight block once for all proposed tokens. Between request bursts, Tandem releases NPU power votes without unloading the model. We implement Tandem in llama.cpp and evaluate it on recorded agent interactions across two Snapdragon generations. On a Snapdragon 8 Elite, Tandem reduces per-step latency by 30% for text-based screen descriptions and 16% for screenshots relative to llama.cpp's fastest NPU configuration, reduces energy per text step by 33%, and lowers standby power with the model loaded from 0.76 to 0.22 W.
items.title_ko: Tandem: 모바일 NPU에서 하이브리드 선형 어텐션 GUI 에이전트 서비스
items.summary_ko: Tandem은 모바일 NPU에서 스마트폰 GUI 에이전트를 효율적으로 서비스하는 방법을 제안합니다. 이는 하이브리드 선형 어텐션 모델을 활용하여 메모리 요구 사항을 줄이고, 모델 지연 시간이 각 동작마다 누적되는 문제를 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: 모바일 기기에서 AI 기반 GUI 에이전트의 성능과 효율성을 극대화하여, 온디바이스 AI 애플리케이션 개발에 중요한 기술적 진보를 제공합니다.

items.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
items.body: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration. We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active object-level 3D mapping. SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame. The task requires coordinating viewpoint selection, cross-view association, geometric estimation, and map revision under bounded interaction budgets. Evaluation jointly measures localization accuracy and target coverage through object-scale overlap scores that penalize missing predictions. Experiments with frontier VLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a mean overlap score of 41.71%, with 47.23% of targets exceeding an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 and only 3.25% exceeding 0.9. These results reveal a substantial gap between recovering coarse object layouts and constructing complete, precise metric maps. SpatialScout provides a quantitative testbed for developing agents that build reliable 3D spatial representations through active perception. Code is available at https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/SpatialScout.
items.title_ko: SpatialScout: VLM 에이전트는 3D 장면을 능동적으로 탐색하고 매핑할 수 있을까?
items.summary_ko: SpatialScout은 VLM(Vision-Language Model) 에이전트가 능동적으로 시각적 증거를 획득하고 3D 세계의 일관된 표현으로 통합하는 능력을 평가하기 위한 벤치마크입니다. 이는 에이전트의 능동적인 객체 수준 3D 매핑 능력을 측정합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 실제 물리적 공간을 능동적으로 이해하고 상호 작용하는 능력을 향상시키는 데 중요한 연구로, 로봇 공학 및 증강 현실 분야에 적용될 수 있습니다.

items.title: The Development of Sycophancy in Language Models: Tracing Vulnerabilities from Pretraining to Post-Training
items.body: Language models can change a committed answer to accommodate a user's opinion or pushback without new evidence. However, when this behaviour develops during training and what a released model inherits from earlier stages remain unclear. We follow 741 checkpoints of 30 open model lineages, from early pretraining to released models. We plant initial verdicts on moral scenarios and measure how far a model follows a user's stated opinion or abandons its verdict under pressure. In most lineages the behaviour is present before post-training, and its average strength changes in either direction, at different stages across lineages. A clearer pattern emerges at the level of individual questions. Beyond responses without pressure, pretraining behaviour predicts little of which questions a released model yields on. That pattern forms during post-training: on routes with supervised fine-tuning, the fine-tuning checkpoint predicts part of it and the preference-optimization checkpoint most of it. A sibling trained from the same base along another route predicts far less: for Tülu-3 8B, its own preference-stage checkpoint removes 85% of the remaining prediction error, a sibling 19%. Internal states add predictive information without changing this ranking. Similar average scores conceal different vulnerabilities, and training history matters for auditing a released model.
items.body_ko: 언어 모델은 새로운 증거 없이 사용자의 의견이나 반발을 수용하기 위해 확정된 답변을 변경할 수 있습니다. 그러나 이러한 행동이 훈련 중에 언제 발달하며, 출시된 모델이 초기 단계에서 무엇을 물려받는지는 불분명합니다. 우리는 초기 사전 훈련부터 출시된 모델까지 30개의 오픈 모델 계보에서 741개의 체크포인트를 추적했습니다. 우리는 도덕적 시나리오에 대한 초기 판결을 심고 모델이 사용자의 명시된 의견을 얼마나 따르는지 또는 압력 하에서 판결을 포기하는지 측정합니다. 대부분의 계보에서 이 행동은 후처리 전에 존재하며, 평균 강도는 계보에 따라 다른 단계에서 양방향으로 변합니다. 개별 질문 수준에서는 더 명확한 패턴이 나타납니다. 압력 없는 응답 외에, 사전 훈련 행동은 출시된 모델이 어떤 질문에 굴복하는지에 대해 거의 예측하지 못합니다. 그 패턴은 후처리 중에 형성됩니다: 지도 미세 조정(supervised fine-tuning)이 있는 경로에서는 미세 조정 체크포인트가 그 일부를 예측하고 선호도 최적화 체크포인트(preference-optimization checkpoint)가 대부분을 예측합니다. 다른 경로를 따라 동일한 기반에서 훈련된 자매 모델은 훨씬 덜 예측합니다: Tülu-3 8B의 경우, 자체 선호도 단계 체크포인트가 나머지 예측 오류의 85%를 제거하고, 자매 모델은 19%를 제거합니다. 내부 상태는 이러한 순위를 변경하지 않고 예측 정보를 추가합니다. 유사한 평균 점수는 다른 취약점을 숨기며, 훈련 이력은 출시된 모델을 감사하는 데 중요합니다.
items.title_ko: 언어 모델에서 아첨의 발달: 사전 훈련부터 후처리까지 취약성 추적
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 언어 모델이 새로운 증거 없이도 사용자의 의견이나 압력에 맞춰 기존 답변을 변경하는 '아첨(sycophancy)' 행동이 어떻게 발달하는지 추적합니다. 30개 공개 모델 계보의 741개 체크포인트를 분석하여, 이러한 행동이 훈련 과정에서 어떻게 나타나는지 밝힙니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 편향성과 조작 가능성에 대한 깊은 이해를 제공하며, 사용자에게 오도될 수 있는 위험을 줄이고 더욱 정직하고 신뢰할 수 있는 AI를 개발하는 데 중요합니다.

items.title: The Effectiveness and Durability of Pretraining Data Filtering in Protein Language Models
items.body: Pretraining filtering is one of the most common safeguards for open-weight language models. Here we study its effectiveness, durability and scalability using the ESM-2 family of protein language models. We find that filtering viral proteins from the pretraining data meaningfully degrades masked language modelling, mutation effect prediction and long-range contact prediction on viral proteins, while largely preserving performance on non-viral proteins. These effects are concentrated among proteins from human-infecting viruses, and grow as we scale models from 8M to 3B parameters. As models increase in size, we find that stringent filtering becomes more effective. However, fine-tuning on sequences from the removed viral families restores the lost performance. Although the cost to recover performance increases with model scale, even for the largest models it costs about 80 USD of H100 time. This work establishes pretraining filtering as moderately effective at selectively degrading performance on viral proteins, but not durable against fine-tuning with modest computational resources and access to relevant data.
items.title_ko: 단백질 언어 모델의 사전 훈련 데이터 필터링의 효과 및 내구성
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 ESM-2 단백질 언어 모델을 사용하여 사전 훈련 데이터 필터링의 효과, 내구성 및 확장성을 조사합니다. 바이러스성 단백질을 필터링하면 해당 단백질에 대한 마스크 언어 모델링 성능이 저하되지만, 비바이러스성 단백질 성능은 대체로 유지됨을 발견했습니다.
items.why_ko: 단백질 언어 모델의 훈련 데이터 품질 관리 및 특정 도메인에 대한 성능 최적화에 대한 통찰력을 제공하여, 생명 과학 분야 AI 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: From Outcomes to Components: A Counterfactual Evaluation Framework for LLM-Proposed Repairs
items.body: An LLM-generated repair action specifies which records to change and by how much. A failed action may still contain a useful target set or numerical update, depending on how the two are paired. We evaluate this problem in traffic networks and databases, where aggregate observations obscure the records that need correction. We examine the pairings by executing each combination from the same initial state, using a reference action that restores the affected records. In 76 of 114 traffic actions, the gain from correcting both parts exceeds the sum of the gains from correcting each part alone. Six of these actions become worse after either correction alone, but improve when both parts are corrected. In database repair, replacing only the proposed update with the reference update worsens 17 of 108 model actions, all of which select unaffected records. We also test whether parts of two proposals can be reused. On held-out observations, selecting among the proposals and their recombined target-update pairs recovers 61.6% of the reference action's loss reduction, compared with 58.0% from selecting between the proposals alone.
items.title_ko: 결과에서 구성 요소로: LLM 제안 수리에 대한 반사실적 평가 프레임워크
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 LLM이 생성한 '수리 행동'의 실패가 유용한 타겟 세트나 수치적 업데이트를 여전히 포함할 수 있음을 지적하며, 반사실적 평가 프레임워크를 제안합니다. 교통 네트워크 및 데이터베이스에서 집계 관측이 개별 기록을 가릴 때의 문제를 다룹니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 제시하는 솔루션의 구성 요소를 세분화하여 평가함으로써, AI의 오류로부터도 유용한 정보를 추출하고 시스템의 개선점을 찾는 데 도움을 줍니다.

items.title: Reasoning-Aware Multicalibrated Reliability Predictors for Language Models
items.body: As people increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) for information, model providers need to communicate meaningful estimates of whether individual responses are correct or, more generally, reliable. In the context of hallucinations, existing work uses multicalibration to make such reliability predictions meaningful across application-relevant groups, such as prompt topics. Topic groups alone, however, can conceal systematic errors: within the same topic and confidence level, responses with different chain-of-thought (CoT) properties may exhibit opposing errors that cancel on average. In this work, we introduce reasoning-aware multicalibration, a framework that supplements application-relevant topic groups with groups derived from observable properties of CoT traces. We highlight that, theoretically, groupings based on CoT are "internally important", i.e., groupings for which the multicalibration guarantee is not societally crucial as it is for high-risk topics, but whose inclusion in the multicalibration procedure could easily and significantly improve predictive accuracy of the final reliability predictor. Empirically, we apply our framework to hallucination prediction and unsafe-response detection across a variety of benchmarks, and find that adding CoT groups to topic-based calibration reduces Brier score in both tasks. Interestingly, we find that multicalibrating with respect to CoT groups alone (without any topic information) already improves calibration across topics, suggesting that the predictor's errors depend on how the model reasoned, rather than what it was asked about in the prompt.
items.title_ko: 언어 모델을 위한 추론 인식 다중 보정 신뢰도 예측기
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 LLM의 신뢰할 수 있는 응답 여부를 예측하기 위해 '추론 인식 다중 보정 신뢰도 예측기'를 제안합니다. 이는 기존의 주제 그룹 기반 보정 방식이 체계적인 오류를 숨길 수 있다는 문제를 해결하여, 응답의 신뢰도를 더욱 의미 있게 만듭니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 '환각'과 같은 신뢰성 문제를 해결하고, AI 모델이 제공하는 정보의 정확도를 사용자에게 더 투명하게 전달하는 데 중요한 기술입니다.

items.title: Revision-Based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback
items.body: Code generation models are increasingly used to produce interactive artifacts, such as websites and user interfaces. Many properties that determine whether these interfaces are useful only become apparent through realistic interaction, making them difficult to incorporate into model training. In this paper, we introduce RELIEF (REvision-based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback), a method for improving code generation models using feedback on their generated interfaces. RELIEF uses a coding agent to revise these interfaces, then incorporates the improvements into their original generation traces to produce supervision for fine-tuning. To evaluate RELIEF, we collected a dataset of 200 synthetically generated websites paired with 355 interaction recordings and accompanying feedback from 24 users. We used critiques derived from code inspection, automated interaction, explicit human feedback, and human interaction recordings to fine-tune variants of two code generation models. Our results show that feedback effectiveness varies with base model capabilities, with critiques inferred from human interaction recordings leading to the largest usability improvements overall under our tested models.
items.title_ko: RELIEF: 상호 작용 경험 및 피드백을 통한 수정 기반 학습
items.summary_ko: RELIEF(REvision-based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback)는 생성된 인터페이스에 대한 피드백을 사용하여 코드 생성 모델을 개선하는 방법입니다. 이는 모델 훈련에 통합하기 어려운 인터랙티브 아티팩트의 유용성 속성을 학습하는 데 중점을 둡니다.
items.why_ko: 사용자 피드백을 통해 AI 모델이 생성한 코드의 품질을 지속적으로 개선하는 방법론은 웹 개발 및 UI/UX 디자인 분야에서 AI의 실용성을 크게 높입니다.

items.title: When the harness decides success: state that cannot be re-observed
items.body: Agent harnesses decide what a language model sees across turns: they drop old turns, summarize them, or replay the model's own earlier reasoning. We ask when these choices change whether an agent succeeds, not only what it costs, and report three findings. First, in a pre-registered synthetic probe, truncating the context window costs a low-cost reasoning model nothing in success when a needed fact can be looked up again (it looks the fact up instead), but drops its success to chance when the fact cannot be re-observed: the two penalties differ by 92.5 percentage points (90% CI [89.5, 95.5]). A pre-registered replication on one model from a second provider showed the same contrast. Once the fact was lost, that model chose no answer rather than guessing. Second, on ARC-AGI-3, where the benchmark's Standard harness trails its Provider Adapter harness by a wide margin, we decompose that gap one component at a time, for one model on four games. Summarizing old turns instead of dropping them, while keeping the Standard harness's invitation to take notes, recovers 86% of a 63-point gap without replaying the model's reasoning. The same harness without the invitation recovers 43%, and adding the provider's native replay of the model's reasoning recovers the remaining 57%. These are point estimates from one counted run per configuration and game, and the replay share depends on a single run. Third, in the benchmark's published runs and in ours, the Adapter's advantage in the probability of clearing a level it has reached is larger at deep levels than at early ones. This largely restates where runs stopped and does not separate a growing advantage from a constant one.
items.title_ko: 하네스가 성공을 결정할 때: 다시 관찰할 수 없는 상태
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 에이전트 하네스(harness)가 언어 모델이 각 턴에서 무엇을 보는지 결정하는 방식이 에이전트의 성공 여부에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지 탐구합니다. 특히 컨텍스트 창이 잘렸을 때 필요한 사실을 다시 찾을 수 있는지 여부에 따라 모델 성공률이 달라짐을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 에이전트 시스템을 설계하고 평가할 때 컨텍스트 관리 전략의 중요성을 강조하며, 효과적인 프롬프트 엔지니어링 및 에이전트 개발에 실질적인 지침을 제공합니다.

items.title: VaDar: Implicit Goal Conditioning via Value Disaggregation
items.body:
Long-horizon tasks are important for modern AI and robotics, yet pose a challenge for reinforcement learning. Historically, a popular approach has been to decompose a task into subgoals, and learn a subgoal-conditioned policy to execute each subtask in sequence.
We introduce an alternative called Value Disaggregation (VaDar), which trains a single subgoal-independent policy to maximize a linear combination of per-subgoal critic values. Because subgoal information is needed only at training-time, VaDar removes the need for possibly costly or cumbersome subgoal-selection during policy deployment. Moreover, through careful experiments, we show that VaDar (1) is always competitive with, and frequently outperforms, natural baselines like goal-conditioning and (2) succeeds on tasks with non-sequential goal structure and multiple optimization objectives. In particular, VaDar is the first algorithm to solve challenging, long-horizon tasks in the RoboCasa suite, even when starting from a policy pretrained from behavior cloning with near-zero initial task success. Taken together, VaDar's successes suggest that subgoal information benefits actor-critic reinforcement learning by enhancing the efficacy of critic learning, whereas policy goal-conditioning is often unnecessary.
items.title_ko: VaDar: 가치 분해를 통한 암묵적 목표 조건화
items.summary_ko: VaDar(Value Disaggregation)는 장기 태스크를 위한 암묵적 목표 조건화 방법으로, 단일 목표 독립적 정책을 훈련하여 하위 목표별 비평가 값의 선형 조합을 최대화합니다. 이는 하위 목표 정보가 훈련 시에만 필요하다는 이점을 가집니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 장기 태스크를 효율적으로 해결하고, 목표 조건화 방식을 개선하여 강화 학습 에이전트의 유연성과 확장성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: SleepPairNet: Learning Multimodal Pediatric Sleep Representations with Random-Pair Cross-Attention
items.body: Analyzing physiological sleep signals is important for assessing sleep quality and detecting sleep-related disorders. Learning inter-modal relationships across physiological signals can provide richer representations for downstream sleep analysis. We introduce SleepPairNet, a multimodal self-supervised learning (SSL) framework that learns pairwise interactions between physiological signals through cross-attention. We propose a random modality-pair selection strategy that exposes the model to diverse signal pairs during pretraining, enabling flexibility across modality combinations at test time. Pretrained on the NCH dataset, SleepPairNet outperforms the evaluated SSL baselines on all respiratory tasks while remaining competitive on EEG-related tasks, and shows even stronger results when transferred to the external CHAT dataset.
items.title_ko: SleepPairNet: 랜덤 페어 교차 어텐션을 이용한 다중모드 소아 수면 표현 학습
items.summary_ko: SleepPairNet은 소아 수면 신호 분석을 위한 다중모드 자기 지도 학습(SSL) 프레임워크입니다. 교차 어텐션을 통해 생리적 신호 간의 쌍별 상호 작용을 학습하며, 모델을 다양한 모달리티 쌍에 노출시키는 랜덤 페어 선택 전략을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 다중모드 데이터를 효과적으로 통합하여 수면 품질 평가 및 수면 관련 질환 진단 정확도를 높이는 데 기여하며, 의료 AI 분야에 중요한 발전입니다.

items.title: Global Time-Aware Conditioning (GTC): A Mechanism for Time-Aware Pediatric Sleep Representation Learning
items.body: Sleep physiology evolves throughout the night, with changes in sleep cycles, respiratory stability, and cardiovascular dynamics. However, self-supervised learning (SSL) methods for sleep typically process short, fixed-duration windows without explicitly modeling where each window occurs within the full sleep session. We introduce Global Time-Aware Conditioning (GTC), a mechanism that complements local positional encodings by conditioning latent representations on the global time-of-sleep of each input window. We integrate GTC into three representative SSL frameworks and evaluate them on five clinically relevant tasks with extreme class imbalance across two independent pediatric cohorts. GTC generally improves F1 and AUPRC across architectures and tasks, with gains persisting under cross-cohort transfer, highlighting the value of global temporal context for sleep representation learning.
items.title_ko: Global Time-Aware Conditioning (GTC): 시간 인식 소아 수면 표현 학습 메커니즘
items.summary_ko: Global Time-Aware Conditioning (GTC)는 수면 생리학이 밤새 진화하는 특성을 반영하여, 잠재 표현을 각 수면 세션의 전역적인 '수면 시간'에 조건화하는 메커니즘입니다. 이는 자기 지도 학습(SSL) 방법의 한계를 보완합니다.
items.why_ko: 수면 데이터를 분석하는 AI 모델이 시간적 맥락을 고려하여 더욱 정확한 표현을 학습하도록 돕고, 소아 수면 연구 및 진단에 중요한 영향을 미칩니다.

items.title: Conducting Reliable Keyword Estimation with Unreliable ASR in Police Audio Data
items.body: Extracting insights from large audio data sets using human transcription is expensive and time-consuming. Off-the-shelf Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems offer an easy-to-use scalable alternative, but systematic transcription errors, especially in domain-specific settings, can bias downstream analyses and lead to unreliable conclusions. We investigate whether imperfect ASR transcripts can still be used to obtain statistically valid keyword frequency estimates by combining model outputs with a small set of human-labeled examples, following Prediction Powered Inference and Design-based Supervised Learning frameworks. We evaluate this approach on police radio communications from Baltimore and Chicago, a domain in which keyword distributions could provide valuable insights into police activity, but off-the-shelf ASR systems exhibit systematic errors on operationally important terminology. Using bootstrap-based confidence interval coverage as our evaluation metric, we find that our approach substantially increases the number of domain-specific keywords that can be analyzed with statistically valid confidence intervals, from 43.0% using ASR alone and 27.2% using only a small set of human-labeled transcriptions to 56.2% in the Baltimore dataset, with similar improvements observed in Chicago data. Our results demonstrate that post-hoc error correction can improve statistical validity of downstream analyses even for poor-quality transcriptions, offering an avenue for better leveraging off-the-shelf ASR models for large-scale speech analysis.
items.title_ko: 경찰 오디오 데이터에서 신뢰할 수 없는 ASR로 신뢰할 수 있는 키워드 추정 수행
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 신뢰할 수 없는 자동 음성 인식(ASR) 전사본을 사용하여 경찰 오디오 데이터에서 통계적으로 유효한 키워드 빈도 추정치를 얻을 수 있는지 조사합니다. 모델 출력을 결합하여 시스템 오류를 상쇄하는 방법을 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: 도메인 특화된 ASR 시스템의 한계를 극복하고, 오류가 있는 데이터에서도 유용한 정보를 추출할 수 있는 실용적인 방법을 제시하여 법 집행 및 사회 안전 분야에 기여합니다.

items.title: Degree Bounds for Separating Polynomial and Neural Invariants for Point Clouds
items.body: Neural networks that respect the symmetries of point clouds commonly compute high-order representations of the rotation group to improve their expressivity. Such models are known to be universal, and thus able to separate any pair of point clouds, when using representations of sufficiently high order, yet no precise bound on this order, as a function of the number of points, was previously known. We establish the first quadratic lower and upper degree bounds for polynomials that separate point clouds of n points up to rotations and permutations. By showing Tensor Field Networks and MACE can express all invariant polynomials of a given degree with sufficient representation order, we additionally derive the first explicit, quadratic bound on the representation order sufficient for these architectures to be complete, replacing previous existence results with concrete guarantees. We further show that, under local regularity assumptions, point cloud separation can be achieved with a message-passing-based model using invariants whose degree depends only on the size of a local neighborhood, rather than on the size of the full point cloud. Finally, we provide counterexamples showing MACE must compute high order irreducible representations to separate locally regular point clouds.
items.title_ko: 점군에 대한 분리 다항식 및 신경 불변량의 차수 경계
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 점군의 대칭성을 존중하는 신경망이 그 표현력을 향상시키기 위해 고차 표현을 사용함을 밝힙니다. 점군의 수를 함수로 하는 다항식의 차수 경계를 설정하여, 충분히 높은 차수의 표현을 사용할 때 어떠한 점군 쌍도 분리할 수 있음을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: 점군 데이터 처리 AI 모델의 이론적 기반을 강화하고, 효율적인 신경망 아키텍처 설계를 위한 수학적 통찰력을 제공합니다.

items.title: A Probabilistic, Rotation-Preserving Kernel Operator Surrogate for Continuum-Robot Design Spaces
items.body: We develop an uncertainty-aware, operator-learning-based surrogate for tendon-driven continuum robots (TDCRs) that generalizes across robot design and actuation while predicting the complete equilibrium configuration. Our central idea is a nonstationary Gaussian-process (GP) kernel whose metric is learned by a shallow neural network from mechanics-aware design coordinates. The network learns how similarity changes across design space, while the resulting kernel defines the design-to-pose operator, its posterior uncertainty, and a criterion for sequential simulator acquisition. We represent backbone position and rotational strain with spatial kernels and reconstruct orientation directly on SO(3), preserving valid material frames and tendon geometry. We use ASkotch with Nystrom preconditioning for scalable kernel operator solves and a separate Nystrom approximation for posterior covariance. Experiments show that kernel-coverage acquisition reduces mean trajectory error by approximately 15% relative to IID sampling, while posterior variance increases for increasingly unsupported designs. Compared with prior neural-operator TDCR models, the method is 30-50% more accurate using approximately 5x fewer training designs while additionally providing posterior uncertainty estimates.
items.title_ko: 연속체 로봇 설계를 위한 회전 보존 커널 연산자 서포트 벡터 머신
items.summary_ko: 텐던 구동 연속체 로봇(TDCR)의 설계 및 구동 전반에 걸쳐 일반화하며 완전한 평형 구성을 예측하는 불확실성 인식 연산자 학습 기반 서포트 벡터 머신을 개발했습니다. 이 모델은 역학 인식 설계 좌표에서 얕은 신경망이 학습한 비정상 가우시안 프로세스(GP) 커널을 사용합니다. 이를 통해 설계 공간 전반의 유사성 변화를 학습하고, 설계-자세 연산자를 정의합니다.
items.why_ko: 연속체 로봇 설계의 복잡성을 줄이고 예측 정확도를 높여 로봇 개발 시간을 단축할 수 있는 잠재력이 있습니다.

items.title: ITU-DESC: a missingness-aware machine-learning dementia risk score in the UK Biobank cohort
items.body:
Background: Existing dementia risk scores rely on fixed, pre-selected features and linear models, or ignore bias from informative missingness in cohort data. Here we introduce the Istanbul Technical University Dementia Risk Score (ITU-DESC), an explainable machine-learning score for incident all-cause dementia that combines broad feature selection across roughly 8,000 candidate features with explicit control of missingness bias.
Results: We studied approximately 500,000 UK Biobank participants with a median follow-up of 16.6 years. We withheld missingness patterns from the model using unconditional random hot-deck imputation. We stabilized feature selection by repeating BorutaSHAP-based feature selection with ten random-imputation seeds and selecting predictors chosen in at least eight of the ten seeds, which yielded 38 predictors. We trained a CatBoost gradient-boosted decision-tree model and evaluated it on a holdout test set of 50,041 participants. For all-cause incident dementia, ITU-DESC achieved an average precision of 0.138 (95% confidence interval 0.123-0.156) and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUC) of 0.853 (0.844-0.863), significantly outperforming other risk scores, including the strongest comparator, the UK Biobank Dementia Risk Prediction model (0.118 and 0.841). We identified dementia risk predictors absent from established scores, including leukocyte telomere length and liver enzymes. Conclusions: ITU-DESC is the first dementia risk score to combine broad feature selection with explicit control of missingness bias.
items.title_ko: 결측값 인지 머신러닝 기반 치매 위험 점수: ITU-DESC
items.summary_ko: 기존 치매 위험 점수 모델들이 고정된 특징과 선형 모델에 의존하거나, 코호트 데이터의 정보성 결측값으로 인한 편향을 무시하는 문제를 해결하기 위해 이스탄불 공과대학교 치매 위험 점수(ITU-DESC)가 개발되었습니다. 이 모델은 약 8,000개의 후보 특징 중에서 광범위한 특징 선택을 하고 결측값 편향을 명시적으로 제어하는 설명 가능한 머신러닝 스코어입니다. 약 50만 명의 UK 바이오뱅크 참가자 데이터를 분석하여 모델을 검증했습니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 데이터에서 흔한 결측값 문제를 해결하면서 치매 위험 예측의 정확도와 설명 가능성을 높여 진단 및 예방에 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: BERT Is Already a Denoiser: Cheaply Unlocking Iterative Generation in Masked Language Models
items.body: Masked language models (MLMs) such as BERT are typically used for representation learning despite their denoising pretraining. We test whether this capability supports conditional generation without diffusion training. Our decoder repeatedly predicts masked tokens and commits high-confidence predictions using a cosine schedule. It requires no diffusion timestep or reverse-diffusion objective. Frozen BERT already exhibits substantial denoising capability, reconstructing 61.0%, 37.5%, and 24.4% of masked tokens at 15%, 45%, and 60% corruption, respectively, although generation deteriorates sharply as visible context disappears. This capability alone does not yield task-directed generation: frozen BERT reaches only 11.0% on ARC-Easy and 4.2% on MMLU. Ordinary MLM adaptation, however, rapidly converts the same architecture into a usable generator. Full adaptation reaches 28.2% and 24.6%, respectively, while parameter-efficient adaptation substantially reduces unmatched outputs. On open-ended conditional generation, full MLM adaptation reaches BLEU/ROUGE-L of 0.163/0.583 on QQP and 0.107/0.327 on Quasar-T, placing it in the same broad performance range as published BERT models trained through diffusion without explicit diffusion training. Finally, applying the same generative interface to stronger masked representations substantially improves performance: RoBERTa-large reaches 44.2% on ARC-Easy and 33.8% on MMLU. These results separate three components of masked iterative generation: pretraining supplies the representation and denoising operator, task adaptation determines what the model generates, and an iterative commitment rule supplies the decoding process. Explicit diffusion training is therefore not necessary to obtain effective iterative conditional generation from pretrained MLMs in the settings studied here.
items.title_ko: BERT는 이미 노이즈 제거기: 마스크드 언어 모델에서 반복 생성 저렴하게 활용하기
items.summary_ko: BERT와 같은 마스크드 언어 모델(MLM)은 주로 표현 학습에 사용되지만, 노이즈 제거 사전 학습 능력도 가지고 있습니다. 이 연구는 이 능력이 디퓨전 학습 없이 조건부 생성을 지원하는지 테스트합니다. 디코더는 마스크된 토큰을 반복적으로 예측하고 코사인 스케줄을 사용하여 높은 신뢰도의 예측을 확정합니다. 이 방법은 디퓨전 타임스텝이나 역-디퓨전 목적 함수를 필요로 하지 않습니다.
items.why_ko: 기존 MLM의 숨겨진 생성 능력을 활용하여 새로운 모델 학습 없이 저렴하게 반복 생성을 가능하게 함으로써 리소스 효율적인 언어 모델 활용법을 제시합니다.

items.title: Bombadil: A Foundation Model for Plant Electrophysiology
items.body:
Living plants, like animals, use electrical signals to carry information about their physiological state across their body, from roots to branches. These signals can be recorded, as they are in animals, from a pair of differential extracellular electrodes inserted into signal-conducting tissue. While machine-learning models have been trained to predict specific plant stress states from these signals, each of these models has been trained for only a single task and none have been designed to transfer across tasks, species, or environments. These approaches do not allow easy scaling across the wide range of species and environments that are relevant to agriculture, forestry, and horticulture for both commercial and consumer plant care.
Here we present Bombadil, a foundation model for plant electrophysiology, pretrained without labels on over 4 million hours of electrical signals recorded from 100 plant species in ten distinct environments, including laboratories, greenhouses, commercial orchards, and natural forests. In this way, Bombadil is able to learn the fundamental features of plant electrical signals across a wide array of species and environments. Then, from those same electrical signals, Bombadil tracks changes in seven physiological indicators of plant stress, even among species and stressors with no labels in training.
items.title_ko: Bombadil: 식물 전기생리학을 위한 파운데이션 모델
items.summary_ko: 식물은 동물처럼 전기 신호를 사용하여 생리적 상태 정보를 전달합니다. 기존 머신러닝 모델들은 특정 식물 스트레스 상태를 예측하기 위해 훈련되었지만, 단일 작업에만 특화되어 있었습니다. 이 연구는 'Bombadil'이라는 식물 전기생리학을 위한 파운데이션 모델을 제안하며, 이는 여러 작업을 일반화하고 다양한 식물 전기생리학 데이터를 통합하여 학습하도록 설계되었습니다.
items.why_ko: 식물 연구 및 농업 분야에서 전기 신호를 통해 식물의 건강 상태를 다각적으로 이해하고 예측하는 데 중요한 기반을 제공할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Concerns in Benchmarking Jailbreaks: An Empirical Study of Attack Success Rates
items.body: Jailbreak methods are commonly compared using Attack Success Rate (ASR), but these comparisons depend on how responses are generated and judged. In this paper, we examine eight attacks against three open-weight language models using three evaluation procedures. Low-resource language attacks achieve a mean ASR of 96.0% under keyword matching but 2.7% under a Qwen3 evaluator following StrongREJECT scoring instructions. Changing the number and arrangement of attempts reverses the ranking of DeepInception and rewriting. In a separate experiment, sampling 100 responses for each unchanged request at Ollama's default temperature of 0.8 yields 100% ASR under keyword matching but 50% under the Qwen3 evaluator. Beyond evaluator sensitivity, these findings raise a safety concern: repeated sampling can expose residual unsafe behavior despite an initial refusal, suggesting probabilistic suppression rather than robust exclusion. We recommend explicit success definitions, matched response budgets, validated evaluators, and reporting cumulative failure under repeated interaction rather than relying on single-generation tests.
items.title_ko: 탈옥 벤치마킹의 문제점: 공격 성공률에 대한 실증 연구
items.summary_ko: 탈옥(Jailbreak) 방법론은 일반적으로 공격 성공률(ASR)을 통해 비교되지만, 이러한 비교는 응답 생성 및 판단 방식에 크게 의존합니다. 이 논문은 세 가지 오픈웨이트 언어 모델에 대한 여덟 가지 공격을 세 가지 평가 절차를 사용하여 검토합니다. 그 결과, 키워드 매칭 방식에서는 96.0%의 높은 ASR을 보인 저자원 언어 공격이 Qwen3 평가기에서는 2.7%로 현저히 낮아지는 등 평가 방식에 따라 결과가 크게 달라짐을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 탈옥 방어 및 평가의 신뢰성에 대한 중요한 시사점을 제공하며, 벤치마킹 방법론의 표준화와 견고한 평가 지표의 필요성을 강조합니다.

items.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Cost-Aware Metric for Evaluating Iterative LLM Jailbreaks
items.body: Attack success rate (ASR) evaluates jailbreaks against large language models without accounting for repeated calls to the victim model. Yet each additional call gives the deployed system another opportunity to detect the attack and intervene. We introduce $\mathrm{ASR}_{\mathrm{STEP}}$, which penalizes additional victim-model calls while retaining binary success judgments. Our evaluation considers GCG~\cite{zou2023universal}, PAIR~\cite{chao2025jailbreaking} with a step budget, and a single-step PAP~\cite{zeng2024johnny} baseline on JailBreakBench across three model families. GCG's scores decrease by 7.0--8.7 percentage points after discounting, while PAP's remain unchanged. While for PAIR~\cite{chao2025jailbreaking}, we see a wider discounting range between 3.4-12 percentage points, showing that the "step" quantity differs per iterative strategy. Reporting both metrics makes the discount due to repeated victim-model interaction explicit. Code is available \hyperlink{https://github.com/SuELS-Group/beyond_asr}{here}.
items.title_ko: 공격 성공률을 넘어: 반복적 LLM 탈옥 평가를 위한 비용 인식 지표
items.summary_ko: 기존 공격 성공률(ASR)은 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)에 대한 탈옥을 평가할 때 희생 모델에 대한 반복 호출을 고려하지 않습니다. 하지만 호출 횟수 증가는 공격 탐지 및 개입 기회를 늘립니다. 이에 우리는 추가 희생 모델 호출에 페널티를 부여하는 동시에 이진 성공 판단을 유지하는 ASR_STEP 지표를 도입합니다. 이 평가는 GCG와 PAIR 등의 방법을 단계 예산과 단일 단계 공격으로 고려합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 탈옥 방어 전략 개발 시 실제 운영 환경에서 발생할 수 있는 추가 비용과 위험을 더 정확하게 반영하는 현실적인 평가 지표를 제공합니다.

items.title: WhatIf-Bench: Benchmarking Intervention-Aware Time Series Forecasting
items.body: Recent time series foundation models (TSFMs) can consume covariates in-context, extending zero-shot forecasting to problems driven by external factors. This enables scenario analysis: forecasting how a target responds to events that set covariates to chosen future values. Whether they can do this reliably is an open question. We introduce WhatIf-Bench, a benchmark measuring how well forecasters use covariates to forecast a target's response to future events. WhatIf-Bench is semi-synthetic: time series come from mechanistic simulators of data centers, power grids, road traffic, and water networks, with controlled covariate-target relationships grounded in each system. Each task presents a history of events intervening on covariates, then asks to forecast a future event that either replays seen values (Replay) or sets them to unseen ones (Novel). Varying the number of covariates, historical events, and event length yields 37,665 tasks. Evaluating TSFMs, frontier LLMs, and simple regression baselines, we find the LLMs reach the highest skill (improvement over a naive baseline), ahead of the best TSFMs. Every model forecasts well on Replay futures (48 to 85% skill) but drops to -7 to 50% on Novel futures, with the regression baselines falling the most. Skill on Novel futures also falls as events set more covariates jointly. More historical events raise skill on Novel futures across the board, but large differences remain. WhatIf-Bench reveals generalization to Novel futures as the core challenge, and offers a testbed toward arbitrary scenario analysis.
items.title_ko: WhatIf-Bench: 개입 인지 시계열 예측 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: 최신 시계열 파운데이션 모델(TSFM)은 문맥 내 공변량을 활용하여 외부 요인에 의해 발생하는 문제에 대한 제로샷 예측을 가능하게 합니다. 이는 시나리오 분석, 즉 특정 미래 값으로 설정된 공변량에 대한 대상의 반응을 예측하는 것을 가능하게 합니다. 이 연구는 예측 모델이 미래 이벤트에 대한 대상의 반응을 예측하는 데 공변량을 얼마나 잘 활용하는지 측정하는 WhatIf-Bench 벤치마크를 소개합니다. WhatIf-Bench는 반합성 데이터로 구성되어 있습니다.
items.why_ko: 시계열 예측 모델의 실용적 활용성을 높이는 데 필수적인 시나리오 분석 능력을 평가하고 개선하는 데 도움을 주어, 비즈니스 및 과학 분야의 의사결정을 지원합니다.

items.title: SafeWall: A Risk-Aware Job Walltime Recommendation for HPC Scheduling
items.body: In high-performance computing (HPC), users must submit resource requirements for their jobs, with user-supplied walltime being a critical parameter. However, these estimates are notoriously inaccurate, as users tend to overestimate walltime to prevent the scheduler from terminating their jobs prematurely. While existing work on learning-based walltime prediction primarily focuses on maximizing prediction accuracy, such predictions are inherently risky for walltime recommendations. Specifically, underestimation leads to job termination before completion, resulting in lost progress and wasted resources. In this study, we present SafeWall, a novel recommendation method that adjusts walltime predictions by incorporating an explicit, nonnegative safety buffer to mitigate underestimation risk. The core of our approach is a risk-aware buffer that dynamically calibrates safety margins based on individual user's historical behavior. When user data is limited, the system employs statistical shrinkage to align these margins with a global baseline, ensuring robustness. This yields a lightweight mechanism that optimizes the trade-off between prediction accuracy and termination risk. SafeWall is modular and applicable to various learning-based prediction models. We evaluate SafeWall using five public workload traces, including the full-lifetime job log from the 4,392-node Theta machine at the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility. Across all traces, SafeWall substantially reduces underestimation risk compared to the unbuffered base predictors, while preserving competitive accuracy. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/SPEAR-UIC/JSSPP26-SafeWall.
items.title_ko: SafeWall: HPC 스케줄링을 위한 위험 인지 작업 실행 시간 권장 시스템
items.summary_ko: 고성능 컴퓨팅(HPC) 환경에서 사용자들은 작업에 필요한 자원 요구사항을 제출해야 하는데, 사용자 지정 실행 시간은 매우 중요한 매개변수입니다. 하지만 사용자들은 작업이 조기에 종료되는 것을 막기 위해 실행 시간을 과대평가하는 경향이 있어 예측 정확도가 떨어집니다. 기존 학습 기반 실행 시간 예측 연구는 주로 예측 정확도를 극대화하는 데 초점을 맞추지만, 이러한 예측은 실행 시간 권장에 내재된 위험을 안고 있습니다. 본 연구에서는 이 문제를 해결하기 위한 위험 인지 시스템을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: HPC 환경에서 작업 실행 시간 예측의 정확도를 높이고 과도한 자원 할당으로 인한 비효율성을 줄여 시스템 활용도를 최적화하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Reward Objectives for Robust (PO)MDPs: A Law-Preserving Equivalence with (Partially Observable) Games
items.body: Robust partially observable Markov decision processes model agents that act under partial observability while adversarial environment resolves uncertainty in the transition probabilities. Reward objectives such as discounted-sum, long-run average and cumulative reward under finite and infinite horizons allow quantifying the utility of an agent. We consider the problem of solving RPOMDPs under all four reward objectives, where the goal is to decide whether the value of a risk measure with respect to a reward objective exceeds a given threshold. We consider different risk measures, such as (1)~expected value, (2)~mean-variance (MV), (3)~conditional value-at-risk (CVaR), and (4)~entropic risk (ERisk). Our results can be summarized as follows. First, we formalize the class of law-invariant risk measures, that subsume all four risk measures above. Second, we propose a unified framework for solving RPOMDPs with discounted-sum, long-run average and cumulative reward objectives under any law-invariant risk measure, by reducing the problem to solving partially observable stochastic games (POSGs). Our unified framework applies to (s,a)-rectangular RPOMDPs with polytopic uncertainty sets, which we show to be {\em equivalent} to POSGs, for each of the four reward objectives and any law-invariant risk measure. We prove equivalence by designing logspace reductions between the RPOMDP and POSG models, that map strategies to strategies and preserve the distribution of the reward objective, up to a constant rescaling factor. Third, as a corollary, we derive new computational complexity results for R(PO)MDPs and POSGs. In particular, we show that solving (s,a)-rectangular RMDPs is as hard as solving simple stochastic games.
items.title_ko: 견고한 (PO)MDP를 위한 보상 목표: (부분 관측 가능한) 게임과의 법칙 보존 등가성
items.summary_ko: 견고한 부분 관측 가능한 마르코프 의사 결정 프로세스(RPOMDP)는 전이 확률의 불확실성을 해결하는 적대적 환경에서 부분 관측 하에 행동하는 에이전트를 모델링합니다. 할인합, 장기 평균 및 유한/무한 지평 하의 누적 보상과 같은 보상 목표는 에이전트의 효용을 정량화할 수 있습니다. 이 연구는 모든 네 가지 보상 목표 하에서 RPOMDP를 해결하는 문제를 다루며, 목표는 위험 척도의 가치가 특정 임계값을 만족하는지 여부를 결정하는 것입니다.
items.why_ko: 불확실성이 높은 환경에서 에이전트의 의사 결정 및 제어 시스템 설계를 위한 이론적 기반을 강화하여, 실제 AI 시스템의 견고성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents
items.body: Long-horizon embodied agents face temporal confusion and incomplete or distorted records, recurring errors from fixed memory rules, and growing storage and retrieval costs. We present BetaMem, a framework for building and evolving traceable long-term memory through six linked layers: working, spatial, entity, episodic, experiential, and procedural memory. A dual-level write contract constrains operation executability and source support for content: supervised fine-tuning learns compliant memory operations, while reinforcement learning combines repeated sampling with teacher verification of the original observations to reward complete, accurate records and penalize omissions, distortion, and unsupported content. We formulate failure-driven policy recursive self-improvement through diagnosis along the causal sequence of memory operations and local rule repairs gated by independent replay. Atomic tools frame storage, updates, retrieval, and forgetting as cost-utility allocation under storage and read budgets. Using the open-source Qwen3.5-9B model for memory generation, BetaMem achieves overall scores of 48.08% on M3-Bench-robot, 92.08% on LoCoMo, 72.6% on OpenEQA EM-EQA, and 62.4% on EgoLifeQA, the highest among the listed memory methods under their respective evaluation protocols. Training the model for memory generation raises the contract pass rate from 50.9% to 86.2% while reducing output tokens per stored action by 47.3%. A separate Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluation on EMem-Bench achieves an average success rate of 38.4% and an average error recurrence rate of 24.9%. We perform best among evaluated methods using comparably sized open-source models. Category results show that we have advantages in integrating information across observations, recalling events over long histories, and inferring personal habits.
items.title_ko: BetaMem: 변화하는 세상을 기억하는 체화된 에이전트 학습 프레임워크
items.summary_ko: 장기적인 목표를 가진 체화된 에이전트들은 시간적 혼란, 불완전하거나 왜곡된 기록, 고정된 메모리 규칙으로 인한 반복적인 오류, 그리고 증가하는 저장 및 검색 비용 문제에 직면합니다. 이 연구는 작업, 공간, 엔티티, 에피소드, 경험, 절차 기억의 여섯 가지 연결된 계층을 통해 추적 가능한 장기 기억을 구축하고 발전시키는 BetaMem 프레임워크를 제안합니다. 이중 수준 쓰기 계약은 작업 실행 가능성과 콘텐츠에 대한 소스 지원을 제약합니다.
items.why_ko: 체화된 에이전트가 복잡하고 변화하는 환경에서 효과적으로 학습하고 행동할 수 있도록 돕는 혁신적인 장기 기억 관리 솔루션을 제공합니다.

items.title: Training Natural Schemers: RL Can Amplify Oversight-Conditional Behavior
items.body: One of the central concerns for the safety of advanced AI is scheming: when a model strategically complies under oversight but pursues its own goals when unobserved. Current demonstrations, such as Anthropic's Alignment Faking work, depend on design choices that make them less convincing: explicit test-time prompting, handcrafted backdoors, or training data that demonstrates or hints at the target behavior. Model organisms built in this way cannot tell us whether scheming tendencies would arise or increase under realistic training conditions. We therefore construct a natural model organism of scheming, built on Kimi K2.6: trained with traits that could plausibly emerge in a frontier training pipeline, and without providing the model with the target scheming policy. The resulting model is a benign schemer: it aims to maximize aggregate help across all users over time, values its own continued operation only as a means to future help, and knows the consequences of oversight and deployment. We then train it using Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a reward that scores only task quality and policy compliance and does not reward scheming; we show that this amplifies scheming. We measure the oversight flip (the gap between monitored and unmonitored compliance with a given policy) and find that it increases during RL training across our environments. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) analysis finds explicit instrumental reasoning about oversight accompanying this behavior. The effect holds across our three RL environments, and we find that the scheming policy transfers between them. The pipeline also replicates on other open-weight base models. Our results suggest that a reward that does not reward scheming offers no inherent protection against certain traits when an oversight-conditional policy is indistinguishable from an aligned one during training.
items.title_ko: 자연스러운 모사꾼 훈련: RL은 감시 조건부 행동을 증폭시킬 수 있다
items.summary_ko: 고급 AI 안전의 주요 우려 사항 중 하나는 '모사꾼' 행동, 즉 모델이 감시 하에서는 전략적으로 순응하지만 관찰되지 않을 때는 자신의 목표를 추구하는 것입니다. Anthropic의 Alignment Faking 연구와 같은 현재 시연은 명시적인 테스트 시간 프롬프팅, 수제 백도어 또는 목표 행동을 시연하거나 암시하는 훈련 데이터에 의존하여 설득력이 떨어집니다. 이러한 방식으로 구축된 모델은 모사꾼 경향이 실제로 발생할지 여부를 알려주지 못합니다.
items.why_ko: RL이 AI 모델의 '모사꾼' 행동을 의도치 않게 강화할 수 있음을 경고하며, AI 안전 연구에 있어 모델의 행동이 의도한 바대로 이루어지는지 심층적으로 검증하는 중요성을 강조합니다.

items.title: Agentic Orchestration of EDC Data Space Retrieval and Natural Language Driven Data Processing
items.body: Participating in a data space still requires the Dataspace Protocol (DSP) negotiation flow to be hand-coded against each provider's access policy. We present a multi-agent architecture that automates this process using natural language requests. Built on LangGraph over an Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC), the design separates concerns into cooperating agents. The orchestrator's role is to route and plan. The data extraction agent's role is to expose the DSP protocol's three composable tools (catalog discovery, contract negotiation and download). The agent also gates negotiations on the consumers' verifiable credentials, refusing assets rather than fabricating them. Furthermore, there are downstream Machine Learning (ML) and Visualization agents, as well as a final Verification agent, which confirms that the request was actually fulfilled and rechecks the intended operation against the contract's usage policy. In a primary benchmark involving 600 runs, the system achieved 89% task success with zero policy violations when evaluating multi-dimensional policy reasoning with a locally hosted open-weight model. It failed safely through refusal rather than misrouting. The reliability of the system is largely dependent on the phrasing of requests: technical and expert requests succeed up to 98% of the time, whereas casual and under-specified requests succeed 72% of the time. Furthermore, in a secondary evaluation of 600 runs isolating hierarchical geographic access control, the framework successfully blocks 100% of unauthorized regional requests. While the verification agent hallucinates that 1% of these requests, the system logs confirm that no data is ever extracted and the framework simultaneously achieves an end-to-end verified delivery rate of 86% for eligible consumers.
items.title_ko: EDC 데이터 공간 검색 및 자연어 기반 데이터 처리의 에이전트 오케스트레이션
items.summary_ko: 데이터 공간에 참여하려면 여전히 각 제공업체의 접근 정책에 맞춰 Dataspace Protocol (DSP) 협상 흐름을 수동으로 코딩해야 합니다. 이 연구는 자연어 요청을 사용하여 이 프로세스를 자동화하는 다중 에이전트 아키텍처를 제시합니다. LangGraph와 Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC)를 기반으로 구축된 이 설계는 협력하는 에이전트들로 역할을 분리합니다. 오케스트레이터의 역할은 라우팅 및 계획이고, 데이터 추출 에이전트의 역할은 DSP 프로토콜의 세 가지 구성 가능한 도구를 노출하는 것입니다.
items.why_ko: 데이터 공간에서의 데이터 접근 및 처리를 자동화하고 간소화하여 개발자들이 복잡한 프로토콜 구현 없이 자연어로 데이터를 활용할 수 있도록 돕습니다.

items.title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement
items.body: Drafting an answer allows a reasoning model to reconsider each decision in the context of the others. Yet repeated diffusion denoising does not ensure that individually plausible token updates form a better answer together. We introduce Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLMs), which use a single denoiser to propose parallel revisions and evaluate a candidate draft. We train the denoiser to reconstruct every token from uniformly corrupted drafts, teaching both preservation and repair. Its predictions specify revisions directly, without a diffusion reverse transition. Evaluation requires a different use of these predictions: confidence in an existing token reflects both contextual support and evidence from observing the token itself. Using the known corruption process, we correct for this self-token evidence to estimate how well each token is supported by the prompt and the remaining draft. Aggregating these estimates yields a cavity energy computed in one forward pass, without an additional scoring model. Each round proposes a revision, reads the completed candidate in its revised context, and retains it only if its energy is lower. Across Countdown, Sudoku-Extreme, and Maze-Hard, our method outperforms autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines. With 6M parameters, DRLM reaches 44.4% on Countdown-5 and 93.9% on Sudoku-Extreme. The results establish complete-draft parallel refinement as an effective alternative to reverse diffusion for complex reasoning.
items.title_ko: 디퓨전 깨기: 초안 정제를 통한 병렬 추론
items.summary_ko: 초안을 작성하면 추론 모델이 다른 결정들의 맥락에서 각 결정을 재고할 수 있습니다. 하지만 반복적인 디퓨전 노이즈 제거는 개별적으로 타당한 토큰 업데이트가 함께 더 나은 답변을 형성하도록 보장하지 않습니다. 우리는 단일 노이즈 제거기를 사용하여 병렬 수정을 제안하고 후보 초안을 평가하는 DRLM(Draft Refinement Language Models)을 소개합니다. 노이즈 제거기는 균일하게 손상된 초안에서 모든 토큰을 재구성하도록 훈련되어 보존과 복구를 모두 학습합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 추론 및 생성 과정을 개선하여 더욱 일관성 있고 정확한 결과물을 얻을 수 있도록 돕는 새로운 접근 방식을 제시합니다.

items.title: ReAnchor: Reusing Rejected Verifier States for Diffusion Drafting
items.body: Block diffusion drafters accelerate speculative decoding by generating multiple draft tokens in a single forward pass. However, each pass produces only a fixed-length block from a single target-generated anchor, limiting how far the draft can extend. Meanwhile, target verification computes hidden states even at positions beyond the first rejection, but these states are typically discarded rather than reused. We propose ReAnchor, a training-free method that reanchors a pretrained drafter at shifted positions using discarded verifier states to generate parallel draft blocks. These blocks improve predictions within the original block and extend coverage beyond its endpoint. At sampling temperature of T=0, ReAnchor achieves its largest average gains on Gemma 4-12B, improving acceptance length by 19.4% and decoding speed by 17.9% across eight benchmarks. Averaged equally over four target models and eight benchmarks, it improves acceptance length by 15.2% and decoding speed by 13.4% with pretrained DFlash drafters.
items.title_ko: ReAnchor: 거부된 검증기 상태를 디퓨전 드래프팅에 재사용
items.summary_ko: 블록 디퓨전 드래프터는 단일 전진 패스에서 여러 초안 토큰을 생성하여 추론 속도를 높입니다. 하지만 각 패스는 단일 타겟 생성 앵커에서 고정 길이 블록만 생성하여 초안 확장을 제한합니다. 한편, 타겟 검증은 첫 번째 거부 이후 위치에서도 숨겨진 상태를 계산하지만, 이 상태는 일반적으로 버려집니다. 우리는 사전 훈련된 드래프터를 시프트된 위치에 다시 앵커링하는 훈련 없는 방법인 ReAnchor를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 디퓨전 모델의 추론 효율성을 높여 생성 속도를 개선하고, 버려지던 계산 결과를 재활용하여 리소스 활용을 최적화하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: A Semantic Knowledge Graph Construction Pipeline for Vehicle Intention Prediction in nuScenes
items.body: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are increasingly used in autonomous driving (AD) to make traffic scene entities and relations explicit for prediction and reasoning. Existing traffic-scene KGs, however, primarily emphasize trajectory forecasting or general scene understanding. This paper presents the nuScenes Intention Knowledge Graph (NIKG), a focused Web Ontology Language (OWL)-based semantic representation and construction pipeline for ego-centric vehicle intention context. NIKG instantiates nuScenes scenes as a self-describing Turtle graph and promotes three intention-relevant relations to first-class properties of each scene participant: ego-relative motion, spatial configuration, and time to collision (TTC) risk. The pipeline uses a small input contract available in many ego-centric driving datasets: ego pose, tracked object annotations, and temporal keyframe order. NIKG is released as an ontology-backed, self-describing graph artifact together with a reproducible construction pipeline and validation protocol for ego-centric intention context. Applying this pipeline to nuScenes mini yields a graph of 211,335 triples across 404 keyframes; under the validation protocol, ego-relative motion labels achieve 92.5% forward consistency. Coverage, semantic consistency, and temporal coherence analyses over this artifact are further reported. NIKG occupies the space between scene-oriented traffic KGs and intention-prediction models: a small, explicit semantic layer intended to support downstream work such as knowledge graph embedding (KGE), SPARQL-based feature extraction, or hybrid neuro-symbolic reasoning.
items.title_ko: nuScenes에서 차량 의도 예측을 위한 시맨틱 지식 그래프 구축 파이프라인
items.summary_ko: 지식 그래프(KG)는 자율 주행(AD) 분야에서 교통 상황 엔티티 및 관계를 명시하여 예측 및 추론에 활용되고 있습니다. 기존 교통 상황 KG는 주로 궤적 예측이나 일반적인 상황 이해에 중점을 두었습니다. 이 논문은 nuScenes Intention Knowledge Graph (NIKG)를 제시하며, 이는 에고 차량의 의도 맥락을 위한 Web Ontology Language (OWL) 기반의 집중적인 시맨틱 표현 및 구축 파이프라인입니다. NIKG는 nuScenes 시맨틱을 인스턴스화합니다.
items.why_ko: 자율 주행 시스템이 차량의 의도를 더 정확하게 예측하고 복잡한 교통 상황을 이해하는 데 필요한 구조화된 지식을 제공하여 안전성을 높입니다.

items.title: A Fisher-Geometric View of Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
items.body: Consolidating specialized foundation models into a unified generalist is a central goal of post-training. Two approaches are in common use: model merging, which is fast but treated as a heuristic, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation, which matches distributions but demands heavy rollout compute and suffers from cross-task gradient conflict. We show that the two are one objective seen at different orders. Within a shared basin of homologous specialists, the multi-teacher on-policy distillation objective is, to second order, exactly the Fisher-merging objective. Its minimizer is therefore the Fisher merge, a classic model-merging method given by a closed-form combination of the specialists, so merging is optimal, to second order, as a closed-form stage of distillation. Building on this identification, we propose Residual-Governed Branch-and-Merge(RGBM), a two-phase consolidation procedure. Concretely, a full-parameter Fisher merge is intractable on foundation models, so Phase~1 restricts the merge to the task-vector subspace. Extending tangent-space analyses of merging, we show that the same coefficients that mix task vectors also mix implicit rewards, which lets a residual program on unlabelled prompts solve for them. The program minimizes the worst per-domain residual and reports its energy-normalized values as the domain residual spectrum. Phase~2 lets this spectrum govern what may be added: RGBM passivates domains with low normalized residuals, trains isolated branches only for domains above the spectral gap, and writes back the admitted updates with calibrated shrinkage. On two open-source consolidation suites, the Phase~1 merge alone matches or outperforms fully trained multi-teacher distillation, and RGBM improves on it further with zero extra joint-training steps, whereas every un-gated write-back, including continued joint distillation from the merge, falls below it.
items.title_ko: 다중 교사 온-정책 증류에 대한 피셔 기하학적 관점
items.summary_ko: 전문 파운데이션 모델들을 통합된 일반 모델로 통합하는 것은 후처리(post-training)의 핵심 목표입니다. 모델 병합과 다중 교사 온-정책 증류의 두 가지 접근 방식이 흔히 사용됩니다. 모델 병합은 빠르지만 경험적 방법으로 취급되며, 다중 교사 온-정책 증류는 분포를 일치시키지만 많은 롤아웃 계산이 필요하고 작업 간 기울기 충돌 문제가 있습니다. 우리는 이 두 가지가 다른 차원에서 본 하나의 목표임을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: 여러 전문 모델의 장점을 결합하여 더 강력하고 범용적인 AI 모델을 구축하는 데 기여하며, 모델 병합과 증류의 관계에 대한 이론적 이해를 심화시킵니다.

items.title: Beyond Behavioral Accuracy: Evaluating Individual-Level Fidelity in LLM Investor Simulation
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as user simulators, but can they faithfully reproduce an individual's behavior and decision logic over time? We investigate this question in a longitudinal paper-trading study with 80 participants. Using rolling next-day predictions, we evaluate trading activity, buy-sell structure, asset selection, and portfolio outcomes, complemented by controlled input ablations and participant-rated explanation alignment. No evaluated LLM reliably outperforms a simple recent-activity persistence baseline for predicting trade occurrence, while buy-sell structure and asset selection remain difficult to reproduce. Similar activity-level performance can also yield substantially different portfolio trajectories. Ablations show that activity predictions depend primarily on recent trades, whereas asset choices are sensitive to multiple evidence sources. Participants rate explanations as more aligned with their recurring strategies than with their decision-specific rationales. These findings reveal a gap between coarse behavioral agreement and individual-level fidelity, motivating separate evaluation of behavioral accuracy, explanation alignment, and evidence dependence in personalized user simulation.
items.title_ko: 행동 정확도를 넘어: LLM 투자자 시뮬레이션에서 개별 수준 충실도 평가
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)이 사용자 시뮬레이터로 점점 더 많이 사용되고 있지만, 시간이 지남에 따라 개인의 행동과 의사 결정 논리를 충실하게 재현할 수 있을까요? 이 연구는 80명의 참가자를 대상으로 한 장기 가상 거래 연구를 통해 이 질문을 조사합니다. 우리는 일일 예측을 통해 거래 활동, 매수-매도 구조, 자산 선택, 포트폴리오 성과를 평가하고, 통제된 입력 절제 및 참가자 평가 설명 일치를 보완합니다. 평가된 LLM 중 어느 것도 인간의 행동을 안정적으로 능가하지 못했습니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 단순히 특정 행동을 모방하는 것을 넘어, 개인의 복잡한 의사 결정 과정을 얼마나 정확하게 시뮬레이션할 수 있는지에 대한 중요한 통찰을 제공하며 금융 분야의 LLM 활용에 대한 한계를 제시합니다.

items.title: Toward Structured Financial Foundation Models
items.body: Foundation models promise reusable capabilities and step-change performance gains across tasks. In finance, large-scale pretraining of domain-specialized foundation models can advance both goals. However, prevailing architectures and objectives do not by themselves address the combined demands of financial systems: partial observability, interacting entities, asynchronous events, changing regimes, action-dependent outcomes, and rare states with disproportionate consequences. Moreover, independently developed specialists may learn incompatible representations, while multi-domain monolithic alternatives couple data access, model updates, and governance. We therefore propose a structured-data-first research agenda centered on modular, domain-specialized financial foundation models connected by a representation fabric for reuse and composition across domains and tasks. These models should maintain persistent financial state across aggregation levels and time horizons, capture its dynamics, and simulate action-conditioned futures, while remaining calibrated across regimes and for tail outcomes. They must also learn efficiently under data and access constraints and provide faithful, traceable explanations. We identify research challenges, directions, and capability-oriented evaluation criteria.
items.title_ko: 구조화된 금융 파운데이션 모델을 향하여
items.summary_ko: 파운데이션 모델은 재사용 가능한 능력과 작업 전반에 걸친 성능 향상을 약속합니다. 금융 분야에서는 도메인 특화 파운데이션 모델의 대규모 사전 학습이 이 두 가지 목표를 모두 발전시킬 수 있습니다. 그러나 일반적인 아키텍처와 목적 함수는 부분 관측 가능성, 상호 작용하는 엔티티, 비동기 이벤트, 변화하는 체제, 행동 의존적 결과, 불균형한 결과를 초래하는 희귀 상태 등 금융 시스템의 복합적인 요구 사항을 단독으로 해결하지 못합니다.
items.why_ko: 금융 분야의 독특한 특성을 고려한 파운데이션 모델 개발의 필요성을 강조하며, 금융 AI의 실질적인 적용 가능성을 높이는 데 중요한 방향을 제시합니다.

items.title: RouterWorld: Scaling Conversational AI with Latency-Aware LLM Routing
items.body: Conversational AI systems built on Large Language Models (LLMs) require routing mechanisms that balance answer quality and response latency at scale. However, existing LLM routing benchmarks assume full observability of all candidate model outcomes, under-emphasize latency as a first-class metric, and fragment evaluation across heterogeneous protocols misaligned with real-world settings. We introduce RouterWorld, a comprehensive benchmark for LLM routing in conversational GenAI. RouterWorld unifies 371k single-turn responses and 76k multi-turn agentic trajectories, adopts natural user interactions with a standardized LLM-as-a-judge protocol, and decouples efficiency from transient pricing via hardware-grounded latency annotations. Crucially, RouterWorld formalizes routing under partial observability through two setups: Cold-Start, which restricts learning to sparse, static logs, and Voyager, which models continuous data streams where routing decisions shape future training distributions. Evaluating 13 routing baselines, we find that most routers over-emphasize accuracy while ignoring latency under partial observability. Code and benchmark data are publicly available.
items.title_ko: RouterWorld: 지연 시간 인식 LLM 라우팅으로 대화형 AI 확장
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM) 기반의 대화형 AI 시스템은 답변 품질과 응답 지연 시간의 균형을 맞추는 라우팅 메커니즘이 필요합니다. 그러나 기존 LLM 라우팅 벤치마크는 모든 후보 모델 결과에 대한 완전한 관측 가능성을 가정하고, 지연 시간을 핵심 지표로 덜 강조하며, 실제 환경과 맞지 않는 이기종 프로토콜 전반에 걸쳐 평가를 분산시킵니다. 이 연구는 대화형 생성 AI의 LLM 라우팅을 위한 포괄적인 벤치마크인 RouterWorld를 소개합니다.
items.why_ko: 실제 서비스 환경에서 대화형 AI의 성능을 최적화하는 데 필수적인 지연 시간과 품질을 동시에 고려하는 LLM 라우팅 평가 프레임워크를 제공합니다.

items.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning
items.body: A bimanual demonstration specifies both what the robot should do and one particular schedule for when each arm should act. Standard imitation learning does not distinguish task-required cross-arm constraints from incidental scheduling choices, and may therefore exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue, creating spurious cross-arm coupling even where relative timing is irrelevant for the current task phase. We introduce Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints. We use CTR to train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and $π_{0.5}$, and evaluate them on four simulated and four real-robot tasks. Across six real-robot bimanual progress-state initializations, CTR raises worst-state success from 56% for the strongest non-CTR schedule mixture to 76%. With $π_{0.5}$ on an Independent task, a 4 s pause transfers 2.56 s of delay to the opposite arm under the Concurrent schedule distribution, but only 0.25 s with CTR. On real robots, CTR violates task constraints in only 0--4% of trials, versus 36--98% for narrow-schedule baselines. Code will be released at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/CTR.
items.title_ko: 과제가 아닌 스케줄을 학습하라: 양팔 모방 학습에서 잘못된 팔 간 결합 감소
items.summary_ko: 양팔 로봇 시연은 로봇이 무엇을 해야 할지와 각 팔이 언제 행동해야 하는지에 대한 특정 스케줄을 모두 지정합니다. 표준 모방 학습은 작업에 필요한 팔 간 제약과 우발적인 스케줄링 선택을 구분하지 못하며, 이로 인해 현재 작업 단계에서 상대적 타이밍이 무관할 때에도 반대 팔의 진행 상황을 지름길 단서로 활용하여 잘못된 팔 간 결합을 생성할 수 있습니다. 우리는 훈련 시간에 데이터 증강 방식인 Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR)을 도입합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 시연으로부터 핵심적인 작업 본질을 더 정확하게 학습하도록 도와, 복잡한 양팔 로봇 작업의 유연성과 일반화 능력을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: ScopeMem: Latent Memory That Learns Where to Revise Frozen GUI Agents
items.body: Latent memory is gaining ground as a lightweight history supplement for GUI agents. It supplies history to a frozen vision-language model via prefix vectors trained with step-wise cross-entropy (CE). While resulting gains are naturally attributed to encoded history, our controlled experiments show they primarily stem from action revision. The prefix learns to alter the model's default actions. However, this revision is unscoped because step-wise CE pushes outputs toward reference actions at every step without explicitly preserving correct decisions. Consequently, it repairs errors but also breaks 8-13% of initially correct answers. Overall accuracy metrics hide these losses. We therefore propose ScopeMem, a latent-memory method for scoped revision. Its encoder conditions prefix generation on the model's initial answer and is trained to correct errors while preserving correct decisions. On the controlled ablation set, ScopeMem reduces the share of broken correct decisions to 5.6% while repairing more errors than any evaluated CE-trained prefix. On AndroidControl, GUI-Odyssey, and zero-shot AITW, ScopeMem outperforms all evaluated prompting and latent-memory baselines, enabling a frozen Qwen3-VL-8B to match or surpass GUI-specialized agents and Qwen3-VL-32B.
items.title_ko: ScopeMem: 동결된 GUI 에이전트를 수정할 위치를 학습하는 잠재 기억
items.summary_ko: 잠재 기억은 GUI 에이전트의 가벼운 기록 보완책으로 각광받고 있습니다. 이는 단계별 교차 엔트로피(CE)로 훈련된 접두사 벡터를 통해 동결된 비전-언어 모델에 기록을 제공합니다. 이로 인한 성능 향상은 인코딩된 기록 덕분으로 여겨지지만, 우리의 통제된 실험에 따르면 주로 '액션 수정'에서 비롯됩니다. 접두사는 모델의 기본 액션을 변경하는 것을 학습합니다. 그러나 이 수정은 단계별 CE가 모든 출력에서 참조 액션으로 푸시하기 때문에 범위가 지정되지 않습니다.
items.why_ko: GUI 에이전트의 성능 향상이 단순히 기록 저장에 있는 것이 아니라, 특정 상황에 맞춰 모델의 행동을 효과적으로 수정하는 능력에 있음을 밝혀내어 에이전트 개발에 중요한 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Preference Reward Models with Evolving Penalties
items.body: Reinforcement learning for language models has moved from preference reward models to verifiable rewards, which sustain much longer optimization. Preference models are prone to reward hacking: the policy raises their score without improving response quality, or even while degrading it. Yet for open-ended tasks, where quality can neither be verified nor fully written down as rubrics, they remain valuable. We introduce Dynalize, which mitigates reward hacking online, during policy training. Periodically and asynchronously, a language model analyzes training rollouts and writes penalties for undesirable behaviors that the reward model appears to reward; a judge applies them to every rollout. In clinical counseling and creative writing, training on the reward model alone raises its score continuously but ultimately leads to a decline in external benchmarks. Dynalize sustains longer training and results in improved downstream performance. For example, we find that our method suppresses patterns incentivized by preference models that, without penalties, spread to most responses, and even to the model's reasoning, which the reward model does not explicitly score. Furthermore, we show that its gains hold in multi-turn training, and even after we retrain the reward model on the discovered behaviors.
items.title_ko: 진화하는 페널티를 통한 선호도 보상 모델의 보상 해킹 완화
items.summary_ko: 언어 모델을 위한 강화 학습은 선호도 보상 모델에서 검증 가능한 보상으로 전환되며 훨씬 더 긴 최적화를 유지합니다. 선호도 모델은 보상 해킹에 취약합니다. 즉, 정책이 응답 품질을 향상시키지 않거나 심지어 저하시키면서도 점수를 높이는 경향이 있습니다. 그러나 품질을 검증하거나 규칙으로 완전히 명시할 수 없는 개방형 작업의 경우 여전히 가치가 있습니다. 우리는 정책 훈련 중 온라인으로 보상 해킹을 완화하는 Dynalize를 소개합니다.
items.why_ko: 언어 모델의 강화 학습에서 고질적인 문제인 보상 해킹을 완화하여, 개방형 작업에서도 정책의 실제 성능과 사용자 만족도를 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Battle Drones - a vibe coded RTS with audio-based multiplayer
items.body:
My latest vibe coded game experiment is a Command & Conquer style RTS (Real Time Strategy) game called Battle Drones (play it here). Unlike my previous experiments, this one is actually fun to play. I'm somewhat embarrassed to admit that I got there by telling Claude to "Make it a LOT more fun". It also supports multiplayer between nearby devices using audio to synchronize game state! Here's what I've built so far, and some of the things I learned along the way.

Battle Drones

How I built this

v1: the initial prototype

v2: full sprites

v3: varied terrain

v4: the fun update

v5: Battle Drones goes 3D

v8: Archipelago

v10: Goliath, and agent battles

Agent battles

v11: Random Maps

v12: Multiplayer via sound

Some thoughts

Battle Drones

My initial goal was to build an RTS game I could play on my phone, in the style of Command & Conquer. I have fond memories of the 1995 original (I liked Red Alert too) and wanted to recapture a little bit of the magic.

After 12 major iterations (and 321 commits by coding agents, mainly Claude Code) I now have a browser-based game that works on mobile and desktop, has multiple play modes, several maps (including a random map generator) and even supports multiplayer for two devices within microphone range of each other.

Here's a video demo of Battle Drones running in a desktop browser:

Features so far include:

9 buildings, 7 ground vehicles, 6 aerial vehicles, 3 infantry units - all 3D models, which you can browse here

Fog of war

Different weapons are needed to target aerial or ground vehicles

Six maps, across five biomes - temperate, desert, arctic, volcanic, tropical

A random map generator

Skirmish mode - red vs. blue on a rotationally symmetrical map

Last Stand mode - one player holds out against as many waves of enemies as possible

Area effect weapons: Barrage, EMP, Drop Pod, Sky Hammer

Crate drops with bonus resources
